questions.q: A dry cell with e.m.f. 3.0 V and internal resistance 0.4 ohms is connected to an external resistor of 2.6 ohms. Calculate the current flowing in the circuit.
questions.e: The current in a circuit with e.m.f. and internal resistance is I = E/(R + r) = 3.0/(2.6 + 0.4) = 3.0/3.0 = 1.0 A. Ignoring internal resistance (3.0/2.6) or using only internal resistance (3.0/0.4) gives the wrong distractors.
questions.p: Current be I = E/(R+r) = 3.0/(2.6+0.4) = 3.0/3.0 = 1.0 A. If person forget internal resistance e go get 3.0/2.6, or if e use only internal resistance e go get 3.0/0.4 - both na wrong answer.

questions.q: A fluorescent lamp in a classroom is rated 40 W. If it is left switched on for 6 hours a day, calculate the electrical energy it consumes in one day, in kilowatt-hours (kWh).
questions.e: Energy (kWh) = Power (kW) x Time (h). Power = 40 W = 0.04 kW, so Energy = 0.04 x 6 = 0.24 kWh.
questions.p: Energy for kWh = Power (for kW) multiply Time (for hour). 40 W na 0.04 kW, so 0.04 x 6 give 0.24 kWh.

questions.q: In Mama Chidi's shop, a 1000 W pressing iron is used for 30 minutes, a 1500 W water heater is used for 20 minutes, and a 60 W bulb is used for 5 hours. If electricity costs ₦60 per kWh, calculate the total cost of running these three appliances.
questions.e: Convert each appliance's usage to kWh: iron = 1000 W x 0.5 h = 500 Wh; heater = 1500 W x (20/60) h = 500 Wh; bulb = 60 W x 5 h = 300 Wh. Total = 1300 Wh = 1.3 kWh. Cost = 1.3 x ₦60 = ₦78.00.
questions.p: Change each appliance time go hour: iron = 1000 W x 0.5 h = 500 Wh, heater = 1500 W x (20/60) h = 500 Wh, bulb = 60 W x 5 h = 300 Wh. Total na 1300 Wh wey be 1.3 kWh. Cost = 1.3 x ₦60 = ₦78.00.

questions.q: A resistor of fixed resistance R is connected across a voltage source and dissipates power P. If the voltage across the resistor is doubled while R stays the same, by what factor does the power dissipated increase?
questions.e: Power is given by P = V²/R. If V doubles, V² becomes 4 times as large, so the new power is 4 times the original power, since R does not change.
questions.p: Power na P = V²/R. If V double, V² go be 4 times wetin e be before, so power go also increase by 4 times since R no change.

questions.q: A trader compares an old incandescent bulb rated 100 W with a new LED bulb rated 20 W, both giving the same brightness. Each bulb is used for 8 hours daily for 30 days, and electricity costs ₦50 per kWh. Calculate how much money the trader saves in those 30 days by using the LED bulb instead of the incandescent bulb.
questions.e: Incandescent energy = 100 W x 8 h x 30 = 24000 Wh = 24 kWh, costing 24 x ₦50 = ₦1200. LED energy = 20 W x 8 h x 30 = 4800 Wh = 4.8 kWh, costing 4.8 x ₦50 = ₦240. Savings = ₦1200 - ₦240 = ₦960.
questions.p: Incandescent energy = 100 W x 8 h x 30 = 24 kWh, e go cost 24 x ₦50 = ₦1200. LED energy = 20 W x 8 h x 30 = 4.8 kWh, e go cost 4.8 x ₦50 = ₦240. Wetin dem save = ₦1200 - ₦240 = ₦960.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the magnetic field lines of a bar magnet?
o: They terminate at the centre of the magnet where the field is strongest
They form closed loops, emerging from the north pole outside the magnet and entering the south pole, then passing through the magnet from south to north
They are straight parallel lines that never close on themselves
They start from the south pole and end at the north pole, never passing through the magnet
questions.e: Magnetic field lines are continuous closed loops. Outside the magnet they go from north pole to south pole, and inside the magnet they continue from south pole back to north pole, forming a complete loop. They never start or stop at a point.
questions.p: Magnetic field lines na closed loop wey no get start or end. Outside di magnet, dem dey comot from north go south, and inside di magnet dem dey continue from south go north to complete di loop.

questions.q: A straight metal rod of length 0.8 m moves with a velocity of 5 m/s at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.25 T. Calculate the electromotive force (EMF) induced in the rod.
questions.e: For motional EMF, e = B x L x v. Substituting values: e = 0.25 x 0.8 x 5 = 1.0 V. This is the standard formula for a rod moving perpendicular to a magnetic field.
questions.p: For motional EMF, we use e = B x L x v. If we put di numbers: e = 0.25 x 0.8 x 5 = 1.0 V. Na straightforward formula wen rod dey move perpendicular to di field.

questions.q: A coil of 200 turns is linked with a magnetic flux that changes uniformly from 2.0 x 10⁻³ Wb to 8.0 x 10⁻³ Wb in 0.3 seconds. Calculate the average EMF induced in the coil.
questions.e: By Faraday's law, EMF = N x (change in flux)/(time). Change in flux = 8.0x10⁻³ - 2.0x10⁻³ = 6.0x10⁻³ Wb. EMF = 200 x (6.0x10⁻³)/0.3 = 200 x 0.02 = 4.0 V.
questions.p: Faraday law talk say EMF = N x (change in flux)/(time). Di change in flux na 8.0x10⁻³ - 2.0x10⁻³ = 6.0x10⁻³ Wb. So EMF = 200 x (6.0x10⁻³)/0.3 = 4.0 V.

questions.q: A straight current-carrying conductor of length 0.6 m carries a current of 3.0 A and is placed in a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T such that the conductor makes an angle of 30° with the field. Calculate the magnitude of the force on the conductor.
questions.e: The force on a current-carrying conductor is F = B x I x L x sin(theta), where theta is the angle between the conductor and the field. F = 0.5 x 3.0 x 0.6 x sin(30°) = 0.5 x 3.0 x 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.45 N. Candidates who forget the sine factor or use the wrong angle get the wrong answer.
questions.p: Di force for current-carrying wire na F = B x I x L x sin(theta), wia theta na di angle between di wire and di field. F = 0.5 x 3.0 x 0.6 x sin(30°) = 0.5 x 3.0 x 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.45 N. If you forget di sin factor or use wrong angle, you go miss am.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly defines simple harmonic motion?
o: Motion in which the displacement is directly proportional to the time elapsed
Motion in which the velocity is constant and directed towards a fixed point
Motion in which the acceleration is constant and directed away from a fixed point
Motion in which the acceleration is proportional to the displacement from a fixed point and is always directed towards that point
questions.e: Simple harmonic motion is defined by a restoring force (and hence acceleration) that is proportional to displacement from a fixed equilibrium point and always points back towards that point. This is the defining feature that distinguishes SHM from other types of motion.
questions.p: Simple harmonic motion na when the force wey dey pull the body back (so acceleration) dey match the distance e don move from the center point, and e dey always push am back to that center. Na this one make SHM different from other motion.

questions.q: A simple pendulum completes one full oscillation in 2.0 seconds. Taking g = 10 m/s² and pi² as approximately 10, calculate the length of the pendulum.
questions.e: Using T = 2pi × √(L/g), we rearrange to get L = g × T²/(4pi²). Substituting g = 10, T = 2.0 and pi² = 10 gives L = (10 x 4)/(4 x 10) = 1.0 m.
questions.p: We use T = 2pi × √(L/g) and change am to L = g × T²/(4pi²). If we put g=10, T=2.0 and pi²=10, we go get L = (10 x 4)/(4 x 10) = 1.0 m.

questions.q: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude 10 cm and period 4.0 s. Using π = 3.14, calculate the speed of the particle when its displacement from the equilibrium position is 6 cm.
questions.e: Angular frequency w = 2pi/T = 2pi/4 = π/2 rad/s. Speed is given by v = w × √(A² - x²) = (π/2) × √(10² - 6²) = (π/2) × 8 = 4pi, which equals about 12.56 cm/s.
questions.p: Angular frequency w = 2pi/T = π/2 rad/s. We dey find speed with v = w × √(A² - x²) = (π/2) × √(100-36) = (π/2) × 8 = 4pi, wey be like 12.56 cm/s.

questions.q: A simple pendulum has a period of 3.2 s on Earth where g = 10 m/s². The same pendulum is taken to the Moon where the acceleration due to gravity is 1.6 m/s². Calculate its new period on the Moon, correct to one decimal place.
questions.e: Since T is proportional to 1/√g for a fixed length, T_moon = T_earth × √(g_earth/g_moon) = 3.2√(10/1.6) = 3.2√6.25 = 3.2 × 2.5 = 8.0 s. The weaker gravity on the Moon makes the pendulum swing more slowly, so the period increases.
questions.p: Since T dey proportional to 1/√g when length no change, T_moon = T_earth × √(g_earth/g_moon) = 3.2√(10/1.6) = 3.2 × 2.5 = 8.0 s. Because moon gravity weak pass Earth own, the pendulum go dey swing slow small, so the period increase.

questions.q: Which of the following radioactive emissions has the greatest ionizing power but the least penetrating power, being stopped by a thin sheet of paper or a few centimetres of air?
questions.e: Alpha particles are heavy and carry a +2 charge, so they interact strongly with matter and ionize it a lot, but this also makes them lose energy quickly and get stopped easily, even by paper. Beta and gamma radiations penetrate further but ionize less per collision.
questions.p: Alpha particle dey heavy well-well and get +2 charge, so e dey ionize matter plenty, but e dey lose energy quick so paper fit stop am. Beta and gamma dey waka pass am but dem no too ionize reach alpha.

questions.q: A radioactive isotope used in a Lagos teaching hospital has an initial mass of 800 g. If its half-life is 6 hours, what mass of the isotope remains after 18 hours, assuming no other process removes the material?
questions.e: 18 hours divided by the half-life of 6 hours gives 3 half-lives. After each half-life the mass halves, so 800 g becomes 400 g, then 200 g, then 100 g after 3 half-lives.
questions.p: 18 hours divide by 6 hours half-life na 3 half-lives. Every half-life the mass dey cut by half: 800 to 400, 400 to 200, 200 to 100 g after the third one.

questions.q: The half-life of a certain radioactive substance is 20 days. Using ln 2 = 0.693, calculate its decay constant correct to 3 decimal places.
questions.e: The decay constant is given by lambda = ln2 / half-life = 0.693 / 20 = 0.0347, which rounds to 0.035 per day to 3 decimal places.
questions.p: Decay constant na lambda = ln2 divide by half-life = 0.693/20 = 0.0347, wey round go 0.035 per day for 3 decimal places.

questions.q: An archaeologist found a wooden carving from an old settlement near Ile-Ife whose carbon-14 activity is only 12.5% of the activity measured in a freshly cut piece of the same type of wood. If the half-life of carbon-14 is 5730 years, estimate the age of the carving.
questions.e: 12.5% equals 1/8, and (1/2)³ = 1/8, so 3 half-lives have passed. Age = 3 x 5730 years = 17190 years.
questions.p: 12.5% na 1/8, and (1/2) raise to 3 na 1/8, so na 3 half-lives don pass. Age = 3 x 5730 years = 17190 years.

questions.q: In Einstein's photoelectric equation, hf = W0 + KE(max), what does the term W0 represent?
o: The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectron
The frequency of the incident radiation
The total energy carried by the incident photon
The minimum energy needed to free an electron from the metal surface (the work function)
questions.e: W0 is called the work function. It is the least amount of energy an electron needs to escape from the metal surface. The photon energy hf supplies this, and any extra energy becomes the electron's kinetic energy.
questions.p: W0 na di work function. Na di smallest energy wey electron need before e fit comot from di metal. Di photon energy hf dey give dis one, any extra energy become kinetic energy of di electron.

questions.q: A photon of energy 4.5 eV strikes a metal surface whose work function is 1.9 eV. Using mass of electron m = 9.11 x 10⁻³¹ kg and 1 eV = 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ J, calculate the maximum speed of the emitted photoelectron.
questions.e: Max KE = 4.5 eV - 1.9 eV = 2.6 eV = 2.6 x 1.6x10⁻¹⁹ = 4.16x10⁻¹⁹ J. Using KE = 1/2 m v², v = √(2KE/m) = √(2 x 4.16x10⁻¹⁹ / 9.11x10⁻³¹) which gives about 9.6 x 10⁵ m/s.
questions.p: Max KE = 4.5 eV - 1.9 eV = 2.6 eV = 2.6 x 1.6x10⁻¹⁹ = 4.16x10⁻¹⁹ J. From KE = 1/2 m v², v = √(2KE/m) = √(2 x 4.16x10⁻¹⁹ / 9.11x10⁻³¹) wey give about 9.6 x 10⁵ m/s.

questions.q: A vernier caliper has a main scale reading in mm and the zero of the vernier scale lies between 2.3 cm and 2.4 cm on the main scale. If the 6th vernier division coincides with a main scale division, and the vernier constant is 0.01 cm, what is the diameter of the object measured?
questions.e: The reading is the main scale reading plus the vernier scale reading. Main scale reading is 2.3 cm and vernier scale reading is 6 x 0.01 cm = 0.06 cm, giving 2.3 + 0.06 = 2.36 cm.
questions.p: To get the reading, you add the main scale reading to the vernier reading. Main scale na 2.3 cm, and vernier reading na 6 times 0.01 cm, wey be 0.06 cm. When you add dem, you go get 2.36 cm.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct statement about significant figures in measurement?
o: Leading zeros before the first non-zero digit are significant
All digits in a measured value, including estimated digits, are insignificant
Trailing zeros in a number without a decimal point are always significant
Zeros between non-zero digits are always significant
questions.e: Zeros that occur between two non-zero digits, such as in 205, are always counted as significant figures. Leading zeros only serve to locate the decimal point and are not significant, while trailing zeros without a decimal point are ambiguous.
questions.p: Zeros wey dey between two numbers wey no be zero, like 205, dey always count as significant figures. Leading zeros no dey count, and trailing zeros without decimal point dey confusing.

questions.q: A student in a Lagos secondary school measures the mass of a metal block using a beam balance five times and obtains the following readings in grams: 50.2, 50.4, 50.3, 50.5, 50.1. What is the mean absolute deviation of the readings from the mean?
questions.p: First, find the mean of the readings, wey be 50.3 g. Then, calculate the difference of each reading from the mean and find the average of those differences, wey give you 0.12 g.

questions.q: A quantity called 'impulse' is defined as the product of force and the time for which it acts. What is the dimension of impulse in terms of mass [M], length [L] and time [T]?
questions.e: Force has dimension [M][L][T]⁻², and time has dimension [T]. Multiplying gives impulse dimension as [M][L][T]⁻² x [T] = [M][L][T]⁻¹.
questions.p: Force get dimension [M][L][T]⁻², and time get [T]. When you multiply force and time, you go get [M][L][T]⁻¹ for impulse.

questions.q: Okon wants to confirm that the equation s = ut + (1/2)at² is dimensionally consistent, where s is distance, u is initial velocity, t is time, and a is acceleration. Which of the following correctly shows that all terms in the equation have the same dimension?
o: Both ut and (1/2)at² reduce to [L], matching the dimension of s
ut reduces to [L][T] while (1/2)at² reduces to [L], so the equation is inconsistent
s has dimension [L][T]⁻¹ which matches both terms on the right
Only ut matches the dimension of s, so the equation is wrong
questions.e: The term ut has dimension [L][T]⁻¹ x [T] = [L], and (1/2)at² has dimension [L][T]⁻² x [T]² = [L]. Both match the dimension of s, which is [L], so the equation is dimensionally consistent.
questions.p: Term ut get dimension [L][T]⁻¹ times [T], wey be [L]. Term (1/2)at² sef get dimension [L][T]⁻² times [T]², wey still be [L]. Since s na distance, e get dimension [L], so the equation correct.

questions.q: Which pair of physical quantities below are both derived quantities measured in the same SI base unit combination (expressed in terms of mass, length and time)?
o: Work done and moment of a force
questions.e: Work done is force times distance, and moment of a force (torque) is also force times distance, so both have the dimension [M][L]²[T]⁻² and share the same unit combination. The other pairs involve quantities with different dimensions or base quantities.
questions.p: Work done na force times distance, and moment of a force sef na force times distance. Both of dem get the same dimension [M][L]²[T]⁻², so dem be the same.

questions.q: A market trader in Onitsha converts the volume of a container of palm oil from 45 litres to cubic metres for a supply contract. Given that 1 litre = 1000 cm³, what is the volume in cubic metres?
questions.e: 45 litres equals 45000 cm³. Since 1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³, dividing 45000 by 1,000,000 gives 0.045 m³.
questions.p: 45 litres na 45000 cm³. Since 1 m³ get 1,000,000 cm³, you go divide 45000 by 1,000,000 to get 0.045 m³.

questions.q: A crate on a rough horizontal floor is pulled by a force F = 40 N applied at an angle theta above the horizontal. If the component of F along the horizontal direction that moves the crate is 20 N, what is the value of theta?

questions.p: To find theta, you go use di formula F cos(theta). When you divide 20 by 40, you go get 0.5. Dat one mean say theta na 60°.

questions.q: Two forces act on a particle: P = 12 N directed along the positive x-axis, and Q = 9 N directed along the positive y-axis. What is the magnitude of the single force that would exactly balance (cancel out) the resultant of P and Q?

questions.q: Three forces act on a ring that is in equilibrium on a smooth table: a force of 8 N pulling due east, a force of 8 N pulling due west, and a third force. What must be true of the third force for equilibrium to be maintained?
o: It must be 8 N directed due north
It must be 16 N directed due north
It must be 11.3 N directed due north
It must be zero, since the two 8 N forces already cancel

questions.q: A wooden block of mass 5 kg rests on a rough inclined plane that makes an angle of 37° with the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s² and sin 37° = 0.6, what is the component of the block's weight acting along the incline (down the slope)?
questions.e: The weight of the block is mg = 5 x 10 = 50 N. The component along the incline is mg sin(theta) = 50 x 0.6 = 30 N.
questions.p: Di weight of di block na mg = 5 x 10 = 50 N. To get di component along di incline, you multiply 50 by sin 37° and dat go give you 30 N.

questions.q: Four coplanar forces act at a point: 10 N due east, 10 N due north, 10 N due west, and 10 N due south. What is the magnitude of the resultant force on the point?
questions.e: The east and west forces cancel (10 N - 10 N = 0), and the north and south forces also cancel (10 N - 10 N = 0), leaving a net resultant of zero newtons.
questions.p: Di force wey dey east go cancel di one wey dey west, and di north one go cancel south. Everything cancelout finish, so di net resultant force na zero newtons.

questions.q: A commercial driver in Kano notices that his speedometer reads 80 km/h at every instant throughout a straight stretch of the expressway. Which of the following best describes the motion of the vehicle?
o: The vehicle is undergoing uniform acceleration
The vehicle's displacement is changing at a non-uniform rate
The vehicle has zero acceleration throughout the stretch
questions.e: A constant speedometer reading means the speed is not changing, so velocity is uniform along the straight road. With no change in velocity, the acceleration is zero.
questions.p: If di speedometer no dey move, e mean say di speed dey constant. Since di speed no change, acceleration must be zero.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward from the top of a cliff with an initial speed of 15 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s² and upward as positive, what is the velocity of the stone 2 seconds after it is thrown?
questions.e: Using v = u - gt, v = 15 - (10 x 2) = -5 m/s. The negative sign shows the stone is now moving downward at 5 m/s.
questions.p: We use di formula v = u - gt. When we calculate 15 - (10 x 2), we get -5 m/s, wey mean say di stone don start to fall down.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between acceleration and velocity for a body undergoing uniformly accelerated motion in a straight line?
o: Acceleration is constant while velocity changes uniformly with time
Acceleration is the rate of change of displacement with time
Acceleration and velocity are always equal in magnitude
Velocity remains constant while acceleration increases with time
questions.e: Uniform acceleration means the acceleration does not change, but it causes the velocity to increase or decrease steadily with time. Velocity is the rate of change of displacement, not acceleration.
questions.p: Uniform acceleration mean say di acceleration no dey change at all. But as time dey go, di velocity go dey increase or decrease steady.

questions.q: A sprinter in an inter-house sports event at a Lagos secondary school starts from rest and covers 40 m in 5 seconds with uniform acceleration. What is her acceleration?
questions.e: Using s = ut + 1/2 a t² with u = 0, 40 = 1/2 x a x 25, so a = 80/25 = 3.2 m/s².
questions.p: We use s = ut + 1/2 a t². Since she start from rest, u na 0, so 40 = 1/2 x a x 25, wey give us 3.2 m/s².

questions.q: A ball is projected horizontally from the top of a cliff 80 m high with a speed of 10 m/s. Calculate the horizontal distance covered by the ball when it strikes the ground. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Time to fall is found from 80 = 0.5(10)t², giving t = 4 s. Horizontal distance = speed x time = 10 x 4 = 40 m.
questions.p: To find how long the ball take to fall, we use 80 = 0.5(10)t², which give t = 4 s. Then, we multiply speed by time, 10 x 4, to get 40 m as the horizontal distance.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the velocity of a body undergoing uniform circular motion?
o: The velocity is constant in both magnitude and direction
The velocity is constant in magnitude but continuously changing in direction
The velocity continuously increases in magnitude while direction stays fixed
The velocity is zero at every point on the circle
questions.e: In uniform circular motion, speed stays the same but the direction of velocity changes continuously because the body keeps changing course along the circle. This changing direction is why there is a centripetal acceleration even though speed is constant.
questions.p: When person dey do uniform circular motion, the speed dey remain the same, but the direction dey change every second as e dey move round the circle. E be like say the velocity dey change direction even though magnitude no change.

questions.q: A projectile is launched from level ground with speed u at an angle theta to the horizontal. Which expression gives the maximum height reached by the projectile? (g = acceleration due to gravity)
questions.e: The vertical component of velocity is u sin(theta), and using v² = u² - 2gh at maximum height where vertical velocity is zero gives h = u² sin²(theta) / (2g). This is a standard projectile motion result.
questions.p: The vertical part of the velocity na u sin(theta). When we use v² = u² - 2gh where vertical velocity na zero for top, we go get h = u² sin²(theta) / (2g).

questions.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 7000 km around the Earth with a period of 2 hours. Approximately what is the orbital speed of the satellite? (Take π = 3.142)
questions.e: Speed = 2 π r / T = 2 x 3.142 x 7000 km / (2 x 3600 s) = 43988 / 7200 approximately 6.1 km/s. This uses the basic circular motion relation between circumference, period and speed.
questions.p: We calculate speed as Speed = 2 π r / T, wey be 2 x 3.142 x 7000 km divide by the time in seconds (2 x 3600 s). Dis one go give us approximately 6.1 km/s.

questions.q: A stone of mass 0.5 kg is attached to a string and whirled in a horizontal circle of radius 1.2 m at a constant speed, making 5 complete revolutions every second. Calculate the tension in the string. (Take π = 3.142)
questions.e: Angular speed omega = 2 π f = 2 x 3.142 x 5 = 31.42 rad/s. Tension equals centripetal force = m omega² r = 0.5 x 31.42² x 1.2, which gives approximately 592 N.
questions.p: First, make you find angular speed omega = 2 π f, wey be 2 x 3.142 x 5 = 31.42 rad/s. Tension na the centripetal force, m omega² r, wey give us approximately 592 N.

questions.q: A javelin is thrown and its horizontal range on level ground is observed to be exactly equal to its maximum height. If the javelin is launched at angle theta to the horizontal, what is the value of tan(theta)?
questions.e: Range R = u² sin(2theta)/g and maximum height H = u² sin²(theta)/(2g). Setting R = H gives sin(2theta) = sin²(theta)/2, which simplifies using sin(2theta) = 2 sin(theta)cos(theta) to tan(theta) = 4.
questions.p: If range R equal maximum height H, we go equate their formulas. When we solve am well, the sin(2theta) expand go give us tan(theta) = 4.

questions.q: A trader's wooden crate of mass 50 kg rests on a rough floor. If the coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor is 0.2, calculate the minimum horizontal force needed to just start the crate moving. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: The limiting friction force equals the coefficient of friction multiplied by the normal reaction (weight), which is 0.2 x 50 x 10 = 100 N. This is the minimum force to overcome friction and start motion.
questions.p: To find the force wey go make the crate start to waka, you go multiply the coefficient of friction with the weight. If you do 0.2 x 50 x 10, na 100 N you go get.

questions.q: A tennis ball of mass 0.2 kg travelling at 15 m/s is struck by a racket and rebounds in the opposite direction at 10 m/s. If the contact time between racket and ball is 0.05 s, calculate the average force exerted by the racket on the ball.
questions.e: Taking the initial direction as positive, change in momentum = 0.2x(-10) - 0.2x(15) = -2 - 3 = -5 kg m/s. Force = change in momentum / time = 5/0.05 = 100 N, since the rebound reverses direction, the magnitudes of momentum change add up.
questions.p: Because the ball bounce go back, you go add the initial and final momentum together to get the total change. When you divide that change by the time 0.05 s, you go get 100 N.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct statement of Newton's third law of motion?
o: The acceleration of a body is directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to its mass
The total momentum of a system remains constant if no external force acts on it
To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
A body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force
questions.e: Newton's third law states that for every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force. The other statements describe the first law, second law, and the conservation of momentum principle respectively.
questions.p: As Newton third law talk am, for every action wey happen, equal and opposite reaction must dey follow am. The other options dey talk about first law, second law, and momentum.

questions.q: A machine fires out small pellets of mass 0.01 kg each at a rate of 200 pellets per second, with each pellet leaving at a velocity of 50 m/s. Calculate the average force exerted on the machine due to the firing of the pellets.
questions.e: Force equals the rate of change of momentum, which is (mass per pellet x velocity x number fired per second) = 0.01 x 50 x 200 = 100 N. This treats the continuous stream of pellets as a steady momentum transfer per second.
questions.p: To get the force, you go multiply mass, velocity, and how many pellets enter one second together. If you multiply 0.01 x 50 x 200, na 100 N go come out.

questions.q: An astronaut floating freely in space pushes against the outer wall of his spacecraft to move away from it. Which law of motion best explains why the astronaut moves backward while the spacecraft experiences a forward push?
o: The law of conservation of energy
questions.e: When the astronaut pushes on the spacecraft (action), the spacecraft pushes back on the astronaut with an equal and opposite force (reaction), causing both to move apart. This is a direct application of Newton's third law.
questions.p: When the astronaut push the spacecraft, the spacecraft push am back with equal and opposite force. Na Newton third law explain dis kind action and reaction well well.

questions.q: A boy pushes a loaded wheelbarrow with a force of 80 N through a distance of 15 m along a straight path. If the force makes an angle of 0 degrees with the direction of motion, calculate the work done by the boy.
questions.e: Work done equals force times distance when the force acts along the direction of motion, so W = 80 N x 15 m = 1200 J.
questions.p: Work done na force times distance. Since the force dey move for the same direction, you go just multiply 80 N by 15 m to get 1200 J.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best statement of the principle of conservation of energy?
o: The total energy of an isolated system remains constant, though it may change from one form to another
Energy can be created but not destroyed in any physical process
Kinetic energy is always equal to potential energy in any system
Energy can only be converted from potential to kinetic form
questions.e: The law of conservation of energy states that energy is neither created nor destroyed, only transformed, so the total energy of an isolated system stays constant.
questions.p: Energy no dey disappear or appear from nowhere, e only dey change form. For any isolated system, the total energy must remain constant.

questions.q: A 1200 kg car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 25 m/s. Calculate the work done on the car by the net force, using the work-energy theorem.
questions.e: Work done equals the change in kinetic energy: (1/2)(1200)(25² - 10²) = 600 x (625 - 100) = 600 x 525 = 315,000 J.
questions.p: Work done na the change for kinetic energy. You go calculate 1/2 times mass times the difference of the square of the velocities, wey give you 315,000 J.

questions.q: A pendulum bob of mass 0.4 kg swings from a vertical height of 0.8 m above its lowest point. Assuming no air resistance, calculate the speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point of the swing.
questions.e: By conservation of energy, mgh = (1/2)mv², so v = √2gh = √(2 x 10 x 0.8) = √16 = 4 m/s. The mass cancels out and does not affect the result.
questions.p: Because energy dey conserved, potential energy for top go turn to kinetic energy for bottom. If you use v = √2gh, you go get 4 m/s.

questions.q: Okonkwo uses a simple machine with a velocity ratio of 5 to lift a load of 300 N through a height of 2 m by applying an effort of 80 N through a distance of 10 m. Calculate the efficiency of the machine.
questions.e: Efficiency equals output work divided by input work expressed as a percentage: output work = 300 x 2 = 600 J, input work = 80 x 10 = 800 J, so efficiency = 600/800 x 100 = 75%.
questions.p: Efficiency na output work divided by input work times 100. Output work na 600 J and input work na 800 J, so the answer na 75%.

questions.q: A wedge is used to split a log of wood. The wedge has a length of 15 cm and a width (thickness) of 3 cm at its thick end. What is the mechanical advantage of the wedge in terms of its velocity ratio, assuming it is an ideal machine?
questions.e: For a wedge, velocity ratio equals the length of the slant divided by the width (thickness): 15/3 = 5.0. For an ideal machine, mechanical advantage equals velocity ratio, so the answer is 5.0.
questions.p: For wedge, velocity ratio na length of slant divide by width, wey be 15 divide by 3 to get 5.0. Since na ideal machine, mechanical advantage join body come equal 5.0.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best explanation for why a screw jack used to lift a car has a very large velocity ratio compared to its mechanical advantage requirement?
o: The screw jack has no friction, so it does not need a large velocity ratio
The load moves a greater distance than the effort in a screw jack
The screw thread converts a small rotational effort moving through a long circular path into a small linear load movement, giving a large velocity ratio
A large velocity ratio reduces the efficiency of the screw jack to zero
questions.e: In a screw jack, the effort moves through a large circular distance (circumference of the handle) for each small linear rise of the load, so the velocity ratio is naturally very large. This large velocity ratio helps overcome friction and heavy loads with small effort.
questions.p: For screw jack, small effort dey travel long circular distance make load move small linear distance, na him make velocity ratio big. Dis big velocity ratio dey help am carry heavy load and fight friction.

questions.q: In a lever system, a boy uses a uniform rod as a first-class lever to lift a load of 100 N placed 0.4 m from the fulcrum. If the boy applies his effort at a distance of 1.6 m from the fulcrum, what effort is required to just balance the load, ignoring the weight of the rod?
questions.e: Taking moments about the fulcrum, effort x effort arm = load x load arm, so effort x 1.6 = 100 x 0.4, giving effort = 40/1.6 = 25 N.
questions.p: If we use moment about fulcrum, effort times 1.6 go equal 100 times 0.4. When you divide 40 by 1.6, you go get 25 N.

questions.q: Why does sprinkling sand on an icy or wet road help vehicles to move more safely?
o: The sand increases the roughness of the surface, thereby increasing friction between the tyres and the road
The sand acts as a lubricant that reduces friction so tyres can slide smoothly
The sand reduces the weight of the vehicle acting on the road
The sand melts the ice and reduces the normal reaction between the tyres and the road
questions.e: Sand increases the roughness between the tyre surface and the road, which increases friction. This extra friction gives better grip, reducing skidding on icy or wet roads.
questions.p: Sand dey make road surface rough, and dis roughness dey increase friction between tyre and road. With dis extra friction, motor tyre no go slip for wet or icy road.

questions.q: A single fixed pulley is used by a market trader in Onitsha to lift a bag of rice weighing 200 N to the upper floor of a warehouse. If the pulley is frictionless and ideal, what effort is needed to lift the load at a steady speed, and what is the main advantage of using this pulley?
o: 100 N; it multiplies the force needed to lift the load
50 N; it reduces the effort needed by half
400 N; it reduces the distance moved by the effort
200 N; it only changes the direction of the applied effort, not the magnitude
questions.e: A single fixed pulley has a velocity ratio and mechanical advantage of 1, so the effort needed equals the load, which is 200 N. Its real advantage is changing the direction of the applied force, making it easier to pull downward instead of lifting directly upward.
questions.p: Single fixed pulley get mechanical advantage of 1, so the effort wey you need na 200 N. E main work na just to change direction of force so you fit pull down instead of lifting up.

questions.q: A block-and-tackle system is used to raise a load of 500 N through a height of 6 m. If an effort of 125 N is applied through a distance of 30 m, calculate the efficiency of the machine.
questions.e: Mechanical advantage = load/effort = 500/125 = 4. Velocity ratio = distance moved by effort/distance moved by load = 30/6 = 5. Efficiency = (mechanical advantage/velocity ratio) x 100 = (4/5) x 100 = 80%.
questions.p: Mechanical advantage na 500 divide by 125, wey be 4, while velocity ratio na 30 divide by 6, wey be 5. When you calculate (4/5) times 100, efficiency go come be 80%.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes static friction as distinct from kinetic (dynamic) friction?
o: Static friction is the friction that opposes the start of motion between surfaces in contact and at rest, while kinetic friction opposes motion of surfaces already sliding
Static friction is always greater in magnitude than kinetic friction for any pair of surfaces
Static friction depends on the speed of the moving object, while kinetic friction does not
Static friction acts only when a body is already sliding, while kinetic friction prevents motion from starting
questions.e: Static friction acts between surfaces at rest and opposes the tendency of relative motion before sliding begins. Kinetic friction, on the other hand, acts once the surfaces are already sliding relative to each other and generally has a smaller value than the maximum static friction.
questions.p: Static friction dey stop motion from starting when body still dey rest. Kinetic friction come be the one wey dey drag body when e don dey move already.

questions.q: A material is said to be perfectly elastic if, after the removal of a deforming force, it
o: returns completely to its original size and shape
questions.e: A perfectly elastic material regains its original shape and size as soon as the deforming force is removed, with no permanent deformation.
questions.p: Perfectly elastic material go return back to im original shape and size once you commot the force. No permanent change go dey for the material.

questions.q: Two springs, P and Q, have force constants 200 N/m and 300 N/m respectively. They are connected in parallel and a total load of 50 N is hung from the combination. Calculate the extension produced.
questions.e: For springs in parallel, the effective constant is k = 200 + 300 = 500 N/m. Extension e = F/k = 50/500 = 0.10 m.
questions.p: For parallel springs, you go add the constants together to get 500 N/m. When you divide the 50 N load by 500 N/m, you go get 0.10 m extension.

questions.q: A rubber band obeys Hooke's law up to a certain extension. Beyond this point, the band continues to stretch with a further small increase in force until it finally breaks. The point beyond which the material no longer obeys Hooke's law is called the
questions.e: The limit of proportionality is the specific point beyond which extension is no longer directly proportional to the applied force, marking the end of Hooke's law behaviour.
questions.p: Limit of proportionality na the point where Hooke's law stop to work. After this point, the extension no go dey proportional to the force again.

questions.q: A spring extends by 5.0 cm when a mass of 2.0 kg is hung from it. If the spring is cut into two equal halves and the same mass is hung from one half, calculate the new extension. (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Cutting a spring in half doubles its force constant, so the extension for the same load is halved. New extension = 5.0/2 = 2.5 cm.
questions.p: If you cut spring into two, the force constant go double. Because of that, the extension go come reduce to half, wey be 2.5 cm.

questions.q: A certain spring stores 0.45 J of elastic potential energy when stretched by a force of 30 N. Calculate the extension produced in the spring.
questions.e: Energy stored = 0.5 x F x e, so e = 2E/F = (2 x 0.45)/30 = 0.030 m.
questions.p: We use the formula E = 0.5 x F x e to find the extension. When you calculate 2 times 0.45 divide by 30, you go get 0.030 m.

questions.q: A boy in Kano hangs a 4.0 kg mass on a vertical spring and observes an extension of 8.0 cm. He then replaces it with a 6.0 kg mass. Assuming the elastic limit is not exceeded, calculate the new extension. (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.e: Since extension is proportional to load, new extension = 8.0 x (6.0/4.0) = 12.0 cm.
questions.p: Extension dey proportional to the load wey you hang. If you increase the mass from 4.0 kg to 6.0 kg, the extension go increase to 12.0 cm.

questions.q: A wide water tank has two small holes drilled on its side wall, one near the top and one near the bottom. Water is seen to spurt out faster and travel further from the lower hole than from the upper hole. This observation best illustrates that:
o: water pressure is the same at all depths
the tank wall is thinner at the bottom
air pressure above the tank affects only the upper hole
questions.e: Liquid pressure increases with depth because of the weight of liquid above a point. The lower hole is deeper, so the water there is under greater pressure and spurts out faster.
questions.p: Pressure dey increase as water deep reach because of the weight of water wey dey top. Na im make the hole wey dey bottom dey spray water fast pass the top one.

questions.q: A simple mercury barometer reads 76 cm Hg at the base of a hill and 70 cm Hg at the top of the hill. If the density of mercury is 13,600 kg/m³, the density of air is 1.25 kg/m³, and g = 10 m/s², estimate the height of the hill.
questions.e: The fall in atmospheric pressure equals the weight per area of the air column of height h, so density of mercury times g times change in height of mercury equals density of air times g times h. Solving gives h = (13600 x 0.06)/1.25 = 652.8 m.
questions.p: We go use the pressure wey change for mercury and air to find the height. If we use density of mercury 13,600 kg/m³ and air 1.25 kg/m³, we go get h = 652.8 m.

questions.q: A hydraulic car jack has a small piston of radius 2 cm and a large piston of radius 10 cm. A mechanic in Kano applies a force of 200 N on the small piston. What force is produced on the large piston?
questions.e: By Pascal's principle, pressure is the same throughout, so force out equals force in multiplied by the ratio of areas. The area ratio is (10/2)² = 25, so output force is 200 x 25 = 5000 N.
questions.p: Based on Pascal principle, the pressure remain the same everywhere inside. If you find the area ratio (10/2)² wey be 25 and multiply am by 200 N, the force wey go come out na 5,000 N.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a sharp knife cuts more easily than a blunt one, even when the same force is applied?
o: A sharp knife reduces the force needed to break molecular bonds
A sharp knife has a smaller surface area of contact, increasing pressure
A blunt knife transmits force more efficiently through the material
A sharp knife has a larger surface area of contact, increasing pressure
questions.e: Pressure equals force divided by area, so for the same force, a smaller area of contact gives a much higher pressure. The sharp edge concentrates the force on a tiny area, making cutting easier.
questions.p: Pressure na force divide by area, so small area dey give high pressure. Sharp knife get small surface area, na im make am dey cut things sharp-sharp with small force.

questions.q: A block of alloy weighs 60 N in air, 50 N when fully immersed in water, and 54 N when fully immersed in a certain oil. Taking the density of water as 1000 kg/m³, calculate the density of the oil.
questions.e: Upthrust in water is 60-50=10 N and upthrust in oil is 60-54=6 N. Since upthrust is proportional to the density of the liquid for the same submerged volume, oil density equals (6/10) x 1000 = 600 kg/m³.
questions.p: Upthrust for water na 10 N while for oil na 6 N. Since upthrust dey follow liquid density, if you multiply (6/10) by 1000 kg/m³, you go get 600 kg/m³ for the oil density.

questions.q: A balloon partly filled with gas is released from the ground and allowed to rise freely through the atmosphere without bursting. As it rises, which pair of changes correctly describes what happens to the balloon?
o: Its volume decreases and the atmospheric pressure on it also decreases
Its volume increases and the atmospheric pressure on it also increases
Its volume decreases and the atmospheric pressure on it increases
Its volume increases and the atmospheric pressure on it decreases
questions.e: As the balloon rises, atmospheric pressure outside it falls because there is less air above. With less external pressure squeezing it, the gas inside expands, so the balloon's volume increases.
questions.p: As the balloon dey go up, atmospheric pressure dey reduce because air dey scarce for top. As pressure reduce, body of the balloon go swell up, meaning say volume don increase.

questions.q: A thermometer is designed with the ice point marked as 32 °F and the steam point marked as 212 °F. If a Nigerian weather station records a body temperature of 98.6 °F, what is this temperature on the Celsius scale?
questions.e: Using C/100 = (F-32)/180, we get C = (98.6-32) x 5/9 = 66.6 x 5/9 = 37.0 °C. This is the normal human body temperature.
questions.p: We use di formula C/100 = (F-32)/180 to change Fahrenheit to Celsius. When we put 98.6 °F inside, we go get 37.0 °C, wey be normal human body temperature.

questions.q: Which of these is the correct working principle behind the use of a thermocouple as a thermometric device?
o: The electrical resistance of a pure metal wire increases uniformly with temperature
The volume of a fixed mass of gas changes with temperature at constant pressure
An electromotive force is generated when the junctions of two different metals are kept at different temperatures
A liquid column rises or falls in a capillary tube as temperature changes
questions.e: A thermocouple consists of two different metals joined at two junctions; when the junctions are at different temperatures, a small thermoelectric EMF is produced that can be measured and related to temperature. The other options describe gas thermometers, resistance thermometers and liquid-in-glass thermometers respectively.
questions.p: Thermocouple dey use two different metals wey join for two ends. If both ends get different temperature, e dey produce small EMF wey we fit use measure temperature.

questions.q: A glass beaker is completely filled with mercury at room temperature and then heated uniformly. Which statement correctly describes what is observed as the temperature rises?
o: Only the mercury expands, so some mercury spills out of the beaker
Only the glass beaker expands, so the mercury level appears to fall inside it
Both the glass and the mercury expand, but since mercury has a greater cubical expansivity, mercury overflows
Neither the glass nor the mercury expands since both are heated by the same amount
questions.e: Both the container and the liquid expand on heating, but liquids generally have a higher coefficient of cubical expansion than solids like glass. Since mercury expands more than the glass beaker, the excess volume causes mercury to overflow.
questions.p: Both glass and mercury go expand when you heat dem, but mercury dey expand pass glass. Na dat extra expansion make mercury overflow from di beaker.

questions.q: A steel bridge girder is 60 m long when installed at a temperature of 10 °C. If the coefficient of linear expansion of steel is 1.1 x 10⁻⁵ per °C, by how much will the girder's length increase when the temperature rises to 40 °C on a hot afternoon in Lagos?
questions.e: Extension = original length x alpha x temperature change = 60 x 1.1e-5 x (40-10) = 60 x 1.1e-5 x 30 = 0.0198 m. This small gap is why expansion joints are built into bridges.
questions.p: To find di change in length, we multiply original length by expansivity and temperature change, wey give us 60 x 1.1e-5 x 30 to get 0.0198 m.

questions.q: A platinum resistance thermometer has a resistance of 20.0 ohms at the ice point and 27.0 ohms at the steam point. If the same thermometer reads a resistance of 23.5 ohms in a water bath, what is the temperature of the water bath on the platinum resistance scale, assuming resistance varies linearly with temperature?
questions.p: We go use di resistance formula by subtracting ice point resistance from current resistance, divide am by steam minus ice point, then multiply by 100 to get 50.0 °C.

questions.q: In the construction of a mercury-in-glass clinical thermometer, the bore of the capillary tube has a narrow constriction (kink) just above the bulb. What is the main purpose of this constriction?
o: To prevent the mercury thread from breaking apart inside the capillary tube
To reduce the amount of mercury needed, making the thermometer cheaper to produce
To make the thermometer more sensitive to small changes in temperature
To prevent the mercury column from flowing back into the bulb after the thermometer is removed from the patient, so the reading can be taken at leisure
questions.e: The constriction is narrow enough that the mercury column breaks there once the thermometer is removed from the body and starts cooling, trapping the expanded mercury above the kink. This allows the doctor or nurse to read the patient's temperature accurately after removal.
questions.p: Di small kink for clinical thermometer dey stop mercury make e no run go back enter bulb immediately. E dey make person fit read di temperature well even after remove am.

questions.q: A liquid-in-glass thermometer is said to be linear because the property used to measure temperature is assumed to vary in a certain way with temperature. What is this assumption?
o: The property varies directly (linearly) with temperature
The property remains constant with temperature
The property varies as the square of the temperature
The property varies logarithmically with temperature
questions.e: Liquid-in-glass thermometers are calibrated on the assumption that the expansion of the liquid is directly proportional to the change in temperature. This linear relationship allows equal divisions on the scale to represent equal temperature changes.
questions.p: Liquid-in-glass thermometer dey work with the assumption sey expansion of liquid dey directly proportional to temperature change. Dis linear relationship mean sey equal divisions for scale dey represent equal temperature changes.

questions.q: A volume of 500 cm³ of ethanol at 20 °C is heated to 70 °C. If the coefficient of cubical (volume) expansion of ethanol is 1.1 x 10⁻³ per °C, what is the increase in volume of the ethanol?
questions.e: Increase in volume = original volume x cubical expansivity x change in temperature = 500 x 1.1x10⁻³ x 50 = 27.5 cm³. This uses the formula for volume expansion of liquids.
questions.p: To find increase in volume, multiply original volume, cubical expansivity, and temperature change together. So, 500 times 1.1x10⁻³ times 50 go give you 27.5 cm³.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a thermometer bulb is made with thin glass walls and a small bulb containing a large reservoir of liquid?
o: To allow rapid and sensitive response to temperature changes
To make the thermometer lighter and easier to carry
To prevent the liquid from evaporating
To increase the boiling point of the liquid inside
questions.e: Thin glass walls allow heat to pass quickly from the object being measured into the liquid, while a large bulb volume ensures a noticeable expansion for small temperature changes. This combination gives the thermometer quick response and good sensitivity.
questions.p: Thin glass wall dey allow heat to enter the liquid quick quick, and big bulb dey make expansion show well well for small temperature changes. Na dis combination dey give thermometer quick response and good sensitivity.

questions.q: The resistance of a platinum wire changes with temperature and is used in a resistance thermometer. At 0 °C its resistance is 5.00 ohms, and the resistance increases by 0.02 ohms for every 1 °C rise. What temperature, in degrees Celsius, corresponds to a resistance of 6.50 ohms, assuming the relationship is linear?
questions.e: Change in resistance = 6.50 - 5.00 = 1.50 ohms. Temperature = change in resistance divided by rate of change = 1.50 / 0.02 = 75 °C.
questions.p: First find the change for resistance by subtracting 5.00 from 6.50 to get 1.50 ohms. Then divide 1.50 by the rate of 0.02 to get 75 °C.

questions.q: Two thermometers, one calibrated in Celsius and the other in an unknown scale Y, agree at a certain temperature. On scale Y, the ice point is 0 °Y and the steam point is 80 °Y. What Celsius temperature corresponds to a reading of 60 °Y?
questions.e: Using the relation (C - 0)/(100 - 0) = (Y - 0)/(80 - 0), we get C = 60 x 100/80 = 75 °C. This is a direct proportion between the two linear scales.
questions.p: By using the formula (C - 0)/(100 - 0) = (Y - 0)/(80 - 0), you go multiply 60 by 100 and divide by 80. Dis one go give you 75 °C.

questions.q: A metal sheet has a circular hole cut into it. When the whole sheet is uniformly heated, what happens to the diameter of the hole?
o: It increases in the same way as if the hole were made of the same metal
It decreases because the metal around it expands inward
It becomes oval in shape due to uneven expansion
It remains exactly the same size
questions.e: When a solid with a hole is heated, the hole expands as though it were filled with the same material as the surrounding metal. This means the hole increases in size just like the rest of the sheet, not decreases.
questions.p: When you heat metal sheet wey get hole, the hole dey expand just like say the hole na solid metal. So, the diameter of the hole go increase as the sheet dey expand.

questions.q: In the laboratory, a thick glass tumbler cracks when boiling water is suddenly poured into it, but a thin glass tumbler does not. What is the best explanation for this observation?
o: Thick glass contains more impurities that react with hot water
Thin glass has a higher melting point than thick glass
The inner surface of thick glass expands rapidly before heat reaches the outer surface, causing uneven stress
Thick glass is a better conductor of heat than thin glass
questions.e: Glass is a poor conductor of heat, so in a thick tumbler the inner layer heats up and expands quickly while the outer layer remains cool and unexpanded, creating internal stress that cracks the glass. In a thin tumbler, heat quickly reaches both surfaces together, so expansion is more uniform and no cracking occurs.
questions.p: Because glass na poor heat conductor, the inside wall of thick tumbler dey expand quick quick before heat reach outside, and dis one dey cause stress wey dey break am. For thin tumbler, heat dey reach everywhere almost at the same time so e no dey crack.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas at constant volume has a pressure of 1.0 x 10⁵ Pa at 27°C. To what temperature (in °C) must the gas be heated for its pressure to become 1.5 x 10⁵ Pa?
questions.e: At constant volume, P/T is constant, so T2 = T1 x (P2/P1) = 300 x 1.5 = 450 K, which is 177°C. Only the final temperature must be converted back to Celsius.
questions.p: If volume dey constant, P/T na constant. We convert 27°C to 300 K, then multiply 300 by 1.5 to get 450 K, wey be 177°C.

questions.q: Which combination correctly states the conditions under which a real gas behaves most like an ideal gas?
questions.e: At low pressure the gas molecules are far apart, and at high temperature they move fast, so intermolecular forces and molecular volume become negligible. This makes real gas behaviour closest to ideal gas behaviour.
questions.p: Real gas dey behave like ideal gas when pressure low and temperature high. Dis one make molecules far apart and make intermolecular forces no matter again.

questions.q: A sealed container holds a fixed mass of gas at 2.0 atm and 300 K. If the volume is kept constant and the temperature is raised to 450 K, what is the new pressure?
questions.e: At constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature, so P2 = P1 x (T2/T1) = 2.0 x (450/300) = 3.0 atm.
questions.p: Since volume constant, pressure dey proportional to temperature. We just multiply 2.0 atm by 450/300 to get 3.0 atm.

questions.q: According to the kinetic theory of gases, the pressure exerted by a gas on the walls of its container is mainly due to
o: the expansion of the container under heat
the weight of the gas molecules pressing downward
the chemical reaction between gas molecules and the container wall
the continuous collision of gas molecules with the walls of the container
questions.e: Gas pressure arises because molecules are in constant random motion and continually collide with the walls of the container, transferring momentum. This is a basic postulate of the kinetic theory of gases.
questions.p: Pressure for gas container dey happen because molecules dey move anyhow and dey hit the wall. Dis collision na wetin dey create the pressure.

questions.q: Two containers A and B of equal volume contain the same ideal gas at the same temperature. Container A has twice the number of molecules as container B. What is the ratio of the pressure in A to the pressure in B?
questions.e: From PV = NkT, at the same volume and temperature, pressure is directly proportional to the number of molecules. Since A has twice as many molecules as B, the pressure ratio is 2 to 1.
questions.p: From PV = NkT, if volume and temperature dey same, pressure go follow the number of molecules. Since A get double the molecules of B, the pressure ratio na 2:1.

questions.q: A fixed mass of an ideal gas occupies a volume of 600 cm³ at a pressure of 1.5 x 10⁵ Pa and temperature 27°C. What volume will it occupy at standard temperature and pressure (STP: 1.0 x 10⁵ Pa, 273 K)?
questions.e: Using the combined gas law, V2 = (P1V1T2)/(T1P2) = (1.5e5 x 600 x 273)/(300 x 1.0e5) = 819 cm³, approximately 820 cm³. Remember to convert 27°C to 300 K before substituting.
questions.p: We use the combined gas law formula. We convert 27°C to 300 K first, then calculate to get 819 cm³, wey we fit round to 820 cm³.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas is compressed isothermally so that its volume reduces to one-third of its original value. If the original pressure was 90 kPa, what is the new pressure?
questions.e: Boyle's law states that pressure is inversely proportional to volume at constant temperature, so P1V1 = P2V2. Reducing volume to one-third increases pressure three times, giving 90 x 3 = 270 kPa.
questions.p: Boyle's law talk say if volume reduce, pressure go increase. If volume come be one-third, pressure go multiply by three, so 90 kPa times 3 give us 270 kPa.

questions.q: A copper rod of mass 0.8 kg is heated by an electric coil and its temperature rises from 20°C to 70°C in 40 seconds. If the specific heat capacity of copper is 400 J/kg°C, calculate the average power supplied, assuming no heat loss.
questions.e: Heat needed = mcθ = 0.8 x 400 x 50 = 16000 J. Power = 16000/40 = 400 W.
questions.p: To find di power, we first calculate di heat needed by using mcθ, wey give us 16000 J. Den, we divide am by di time 40 seconds to get 400 W.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly states the SI unit of specific heat capacity?
questions.e: Specific heat capacity is heat per unit mass per unit temperature rise, so its unit is J/kg°C.
questions.p: Specific heat capacity mean amount of heat per unit mass per unit temperature change. Dat na why di unit be J/kg°C.

questions.q: A student heats 0.2 kg of a liquid using a 50 W heater for 5 minutes. The temperature rises from 24°C to 84°C. Calculate the specific heat capacity of the liquid, assuming all heat supplied is absorbed by the liquid.
questions.e: Heat supplied = Power x time = 50 x 300 = 15000 J. Specific heat capacity c = Q/(mθ) = 15000/(0.2 x 60) = 1250 J/kg°C.
questions.p: We multiply di 50 W power by 300 seconds to get di total heat supplied as 15000 J. If we divide am by mass and temperature rise, we go get 1250 J/kg°C.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes what happens to the temperature of a pure substance during melting at its melting point, while heat is still being supplied?
o: The temperature rises then falls sharply
The temperature remains constant until melting is complete
questions.e: During a change of state, supplied heat is used to break molecular bonds (latent heat), not to raise temperature, so temperature stays constant until melting ends.
questions.p: When substance dey melt, all di heat wey you dey put inside dey break bond, e no dey increase temperature. Dat na why temperature remain constant until everything finish melting.

questions.q: A 1.0 kW electric kettle contains 0.6 kg of water at 100°C. If the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is 2.3 x 10⁶ J/kg, how long will it take to boil away 0.1 kg of the water completely, assuming all heat goes into vaporization?
questions.e: Heat needed = mL = 0.1 x 2.3x10⁶ = 230000 J. Time = Heat/Power = 230000/1000 = 230 s.
questions.p: We multiply di mass 0.1 kg by di latent heat 2.3 x 10⁶ J/kg to get 230000 J. When we divide am by di power of 1000 W, we get 230 s.

questions.q: Two solid blocks, P and Q, of equal mass are supplied with equal quantities of heat energy. Block P shows a greater rise in temperature than block Q. What can be correctly concluded about the two blocks?
o: P and Q have the same specific heat capacity
P has a higher melting point than Q
P has a higher specific heat capacity than Q
P has a lower specific heat capacity than Q
questions.e: Since Q = mcθ, for the same mass and heat supplied, a smaller temperature rise means a larger specific heat capacity. P rises more, so P must have the lower specific heat capacity.
questions.p: If temperature rise high well well for block P when same heat enter, e mean say block P no sabi pack heat like block Q. So, P get lower specific heat capacity.

questions.q: Which arrangement best explains why a thermos flask (vacuum flask) keeps a drink hot for several hours?
o: The vacuum between the walls prevents conduction and convection, while the silvered surfaces reduce radiation
The flask is made thick to block all forms of heat transfer completely
The cork stopper conducts heat back into the flask
The double wall is painted black to absorb heat and keep it inside
questions.e: A vacuum flask has an evacuated space that stops conduction and convection, and silvered walls that reflect radiant heat back. This combination minimizes all three modes of heat loss.
questions.p: Vacuum flask get empty space wey dey stop conduction and convection, come get silvered wall wey dey send radiant heat back. Dis one dey make sure say heat no escape easily.

questions.q: A student heats one end of a uniform metal rod and notices that wax placed at equal intervals along the rod melts one after another, starting from the heated end. What does this observation best demonstrate?
o: Heat travels through the rod by radiation only
Heat travels through the rod by convection currents
The rod has a negative temperature coefficient of resistance
Heat travels through the rod by conduction, moving from hotter to cooler regions
questions.e: The successive melting of wax shows heat being passed from particle to particle along the solid rod, which is conduction. Convection needs a fluid, and radiation does not require this particle-to-particle contact.
questions.p: When wax dey melt one after another from where dem heat am, e show say heat dey waka pass solid iron from one molecule go another, and na conduction be dat.

questions.q: A room is heated by a radiator placed near the floor on one side of the room. Explain why this position is more effective than placing the radiator near the ceiling.
o: Heat from a radiator only travels downward due to gravity
Placing the radiator near the floor increases conduction through the floor tiles
Heated air near the floor rises, setting up a convection current that circulates warm air throughout the room
Radiators placed near the ceiling cannot radiate heat effectively
questions.e: Air heated near the floor expands, becomes less dense, and rises, while cooler air sinks to replace it, creating a convection current that warms the whole room. A radiator near the ceiling would only heat air that stays at the top.
questions.p: Hot air near floor dey light, so e dey go up while cold air dey come down, con form convection current wey dey warm everywhere. If e dey top, na only roof go warm.

questions.q: Two identical rods, X and Y, of the same length and cross-sectional area are joined end to end to form a single composite rod. The thermal conductivity of X is 200 W/m K and that of Y is 100 W/m K. If the free end of X is kept at 80°C and the free end of Y at 20°C, which statement about the junction temperature is correct?
o: The junction temperature is exactly 50°C, the average of both ends
The junction temperature is closer to 80°C because X conducts heat faster
The junction temperature is closer to 20°C because Y conducts heat faster
The junction temperature is lower than 20°C due to heat loss
questions.e: At steady state, the same heat current flows through both rods, so kA(T1-Tj)/L for X equals kB(Tj-T2)/L for Y. Since X conducts better, less temperature drop occurs across it, making the junction temperature closer to 80°C than to 20°C.
questions.p: Because rod X get high thermal conductivity pass Y, heat go flow fast for X. Dis mean say junction temperature go near 80°C pass 20°C.

questions.q: A solar water heater panel is painted matt black instead of white or silver. Which property of the black surface makes it suitable for this purpose?
o: Black surfaces are better absorbers and emitters of radiant heat than light-coloured surfaces
Black surfaces reflect more radiation than light-coloured surfaces
Black surfaces prevent convection currents from forming in the water
Black surfaces have lower thermal conductivity than light-coloured surfaces
questions.e: Dull black surfaces absorb radiant heat energy much better than shiny or light-coloured surfaces, which mostly reflect it. This makes black paint ideal for capturing solar radiation in a water heater.
questions.p: Black colour dey absorb sun heat well well pass white or shiny surface. Dat na why dem dey paint solar panel black make e fit catch heat sharp sharp.

questions.q: A point source of heat radiates energy uniformly in all directions. At a distance of 2.0 m from the source, the intensity of radiation is 50 W/m². Using the inverse square law, calculate the intensity of radiation at a distance of 4.0 m from the same source.
questions.e: Intensity follows an inverse square law, I is proportional to 1/r². Doubling the distance from 2.0 m to 4.0 m reduces intensity by a factor of 4, so new intensity = 50/4 = 12.5 W/m².
questions.p: Radiation intensity dey follow inverse square law, meaning say as distance double from 2.0 m to 4.0 m, intensity go reduce by four. So 50 W/m² divide by 4 give us 12.5 W/m².

questions.q: A rope is tied to a wall and Chidinma shakes the free end up and down, sending a wave along the rope. The particles of the rope move up and down while the wave itself travels horizontally toward the wall. This wave is best classified as:
questions.e: The rope particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction the wave travels, which is the definition of a transverse wave. Sound and longitudinal waves have particle motion parallel to wave travel, so they do not fit here.
questions.p: As the rope particles dey move up and down while the wave dey travel forward, that one na transverse wave. Longitudinal waves dey move parallel to the direction of the wave, so e no fit be that one.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why mechanical waves, unlike electromagnetic waves, cannot travel through a vacuum?
o: Mechanical waves travel faster than electromagnetic waves only in air
Mechanical waves require a material medium whose particles vibrate to transfer energy
Electromagnetic waves have infinite wavelength in a vacuum
Mechanical waves have no frequency in a vacuum
questions.e: Mechanical waves such as sound and water waves transfer energy by making medium particles vibrate, so without a medium there is nothing to vibrate. Electromagnetic waves transfer energy through oscillating electric and magnetic fields, needing no medium.
questions.p: Mechanical waves need particles for medium to carry energy, so if no medium dey, nothing go vibrate. Electromagnetic waves no need medium because dem dey use electric and magnetic fields.

questions.q: A water wave travels from a deep region into a shallower region of a ripple tank at an angle to the boundary. Which property of the wave changes as a result of this refraction?
o: Speed and wavelength, but not frequency
Frequency and speed, but not wavelength
questions.e: When a wave crosses into a region of different depth, its speed and wavelength change because they depend on the medium, but the frequency stays the same since it is fixed by the source. This is a standard feature of wave refraction.
questions.p: When wave enter shallow water, the speed and wavelength go change, but the frequency no go change because na the source determine am. This one na wetin dey happen for refraction.

questions.q: A stretched spring (slinky) is pushed and pulled back and forth along its own length, producing regions where coils are squeezed together (compressions) and regions where they are spread apart (rarefactions). This type of wave is called:
questions.e: In this wave, the coils vibrate back and forth along the same direction as the wave travels, creating compressions and rarefactions. This is the defining feature of a longitudinal wave.
questions.p: When the coils move back and forth for the same direction as the wave, we dey call am longitudinal wave. The compressions and rarefactions na wetin show say the wave dey travel like that.

questions.q: A ripple tank generator produces plane water waves of wavelength 1.2 cm, which travel a distance of 60 cm in 5 seconds. Calculate the frequency of the waves.
questions.e: Speed = distance/time = 60/5 = 12 cm/s. Frequency = speed/wavelength = 12/1.2 = 10 Hz.
questions.p: First, we find speed by dividing distance 60 cm by time 5 s to get 12 cm/s. Then, we divide the speed by wavelength 1.2 cm to get 10 Hz.

questions.q: A progressive wave travelling along a long rope has its displacement-time graph and displacement-distance graph both showing a complete cycle. If the wave takes 0.25 s to complete one oscillation and covers a distance of 2 m in that same time, calculate the wavelength of the wave.
questions.e: In one period (0.25 s), the wave advances exactly one wavelength, which is the distance it covers in that time. Since the wave moves 2 m in 0.25 s, the wavelength is 2 m.
questions.p: The time e take to complete one oscillation na the period. Since the wave travel 2 m for that same time, that distance na the wavelength.

questions.q: A stationary (standing) wave is formed on a string fixed at both ends. Which of the following correctly describes the points of zero displacement along the string?
o: Antinodes, which move along the string as time passes
Nodes, which occur only at the midpoint of the string regardless of the mode of vibration
Nodes, which occur where the two travelling waves always interfere destructively
Antinodes, which occur where the two travelling waves always interfere constructively
questions.e: A stationary wave is formed by two identical waves travelling in opposite directions, and at certain fixed points they always meet out of phase, cancelling to give zero displacement; these are called nodes. Antinodes are the points of maximum displacement, not zero displacement.
questions.p: For stationary wave, the points where displacement dey zero na nodes, because the waves dey cancel each other out. Antinodes na the points where the displacement dey maximum.

questions.q: A boy standing 170 m away from a tall warehouse wall at Apapa claps once. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, how long after the clap will he hear the echo?
questions.e: The sound travels to the wall and back, a distance of 2 x 170 = 340 m. Time = distance/speed = 340/340 = 1.0 s.
questions.p: The sound must go go the wall and come back, meaning say distance na 2 x 170 = 340 m. If you divide distance by speed, you go get 340/340 = 1.0 s.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a soldier far away is seen to fire a gun before the sound of the gunshot is heard?
o: The speed of light is far greater than the speed of sound in air
Sound waves are absorbed by air before reaching the observer
Light travels through a vacuum but sound cannot
Light waves have a higher frequency than sound waves
questions.e: Light travels at about 3 x 10⁸ m/s while sound travels at about 340 m/s in air, so light reaches the observer almost instantly while sound takes a noticeable time.
questions.p: Light dey travel fast well well, about 3 x 10⁸ m/s, while sound dey move slow for air, about 340 m/s. Na why you go see light quick quick before you hear the gunshot sound.

questions.q: Two sound waves of frequencies 512 Hz and 516 Hz are produced together from two sources near Kano market. What phenomenon is produced, and what is its frequency?
questions.e: When two sounds of slightly different frequencies are produced together, beats occur. The beat frequency equals the difference between the two frequencies, 516 - 512 = 4 Hz.
questions.p: When two sound wey get small difference for frequency play together, beats dey happen. You go just subtract the two frequencies, 516 minus 512, to get 4 Hz.

questions.q: A student standing between two parallel walls claps his hands and notices that the clap sound is prolonged and gradually fades rather than being heard as separate distinct echoes. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.e: Reverberation is the persistence of sound due to multiple reflections that arrive too close together in time to be heard as separate echoes, unlike a true distinct echo.
questions.p: When sound dey reflect plenty times and e dey stay for air too long instead make e clear like separate echo, we dey call am reverberation.

questions.q: A simple pendulum of length 0.9 m is set swinging close to a second identical pendulum of the same length hanging freely nearby, both suspended from the same rigid support. After some time, the second pendulum is observed to start swinging with increasing amplitude even though it was not touched. What principle explains this observation?
o: Resonance due to matching natural frequencies
questions.e: Since both pendulums have the same length, they share the same natural frequency. Vibrations transmitted through the support drive the second pendulum at its natural frequency, causing resonance and growing amplitude.
questions.p: Because both pendulums get the same length, dem dey share the same natural frequency. This one dey cause resonance make the second pendulum start to swing well well.

questions.q: An open pipe and a closed pipe have the same length. If the speed of sound in air is the same for both, how does the fundamental frequency of the open pipe compare with that of the closed pipe?
o: It is equal to the frequency of the closed pipe
It is four times the frequency of the closed pipe
It is half the frequency of the closed pipe
It is twice the frequency of the closed pipe
questions.e: For a closed pipe of length L, fundamental frequency is v/4L, while for an open pipe of the same length it is v/2L. Dividing shows the open pipe's fundamental is twice that of the closed pipe.
questions.p: Closed pipe formula na v/4L, but open pipe formula na v/2L. When you check am, the fundamental frequency of the open pipe bi twice the closed pipe own.

questions.q: A concave mirror forms a virtual, upright and magnified image of an object. Where must the object be placed relative to the mirror?
o: Between the pole and the focal point
questions.e: A concave mirror gives a virtual, upright, magnified image only when the object is placed between the pole and the focus. Beyond the focus, images are real and inverted.
questions.p: Na only when you put object between the pole and the focus of concave mirror you go get virtual, upright and big image. Once you move am go beyond focus, the image go turn real and upside down.

questions.q: Which property of light is responsible for a plane mirror forming an image that is the same size as the object and appears as far behind the mirror as the object is in front?
o: Refraction of light at the mirror surface
Reflection of light obeying the laws of reflection
Dispersion of light into its components
Diffraction of light at the mirror edges
questions.e: Plane mirror images are formed because reflected rays obey the laws of reflection, with the angle of incidence equal to the angle of reflection. This geometry makes image distance equal to object distance.
questions.p: Na as light dey reflect follow law of reflection wey say angle of incidence equal angle of reflection make plane mirror form image wey dey same size with object and dey inside mirror.

questions.q: A convex mirror used as a car side mirror has a focal length of 20 cm. An object is placed 60 cm from the mirror. Calculate the magnification of the image formed.
questions.e: For a convex mirror, f = +20 cm, u = -60 cm. Using 1/v = 1/f - 1/u: 1/v = 1/20 + 1/60 = 4/60, so v = 15 cm. Magnification = v/u in magnitude = 15/60 = 1/4.
questions.p: For convex mirror, we use f = +20 cm and u = -60 cm inside mirror formula to find v = 15 cm. Magnification na v over u, wey give us 15/60 wey be 1/4.

questions.q: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror and is reflected such that the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is 80°. What is the angle of incidence?
questions.e: Since the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, the two angles together make 80°, so each angle is 80/2 = 40°.
questions.p: Since angle of incidence and angle of reflection must dey equal, and both of them join together give 80°, you just divide 80° by 2 to get 40°.

questions.q: Why is a convex mirror commonly fixed at sharp bends on Nigerian roads to help drivers see oncoming vehicles?
o: It focuses all incoming rays to a single point in front of the mirror
It forms a real image that can be projected onto a screen for drivers
It gives a diminished, upright image and has a wide field of view
It produces a magnified image that shows fine details of distant cars
questions.e: A convex mirror always forms a diminished, upright, virtual image regardless of object distance, and its curved shape allows it to capture a wider field of view. This helps drivers see more of the road at bends.
questions.p: Convex mirror dey show small and upright image, plus e get wide field of view. Naim make drivers dey use am for sharp bend make dem fit see motor wey dey come.

questions.q: A ray of light travelling in water (refractive index 4/3) strikes the water-air boundary at an angle of incidence of 60°. Given that sin 60° = 0.87, determine whether the ray undergoes total internal reflection, given the critical angle for water-air is about 48.6°.
o: The ray travels straight through without bending
The ray is totally internally reflected because the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle
The ray is absorbed completely at the boundary
The ray refracts into the air because the angle of incidence is less than the critical angle
questions.e: The critical angle for water-air is about 48.6°. Since the angle of incidence (60°) is greater than this critical angle, the light cannot refract out and is totally internally reflected back into the water.
questions.p: Critical angle for water-air na 48.6°. Since 60° pass 48.6°, light no fit comot go air, e go just bounce back inside water.

questions.q: A thin diverging (concave) lens has a focal length of 20 cm. An object is placed 30 cm in front of it. Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u (real-is-positive convention, with f negative for diverging lens), calculate the image distance.
questions.e: For a diverging lens, f = -20 cm and u = -30 cm (object distance, real-is-positive sign convention). Using 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = -1/20 - 1/30 = -5/60, so v = -12 cm, meaning a virtual image forms 12 cm in front of the lens.
questions.p: For diverging lens, f na -20 cm and u na -30 cm. When you calculate 1/v = 1/f + 1/u, you go get -12 cm, wey mean say image dey virtual and e dey front of lens.
