questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the image formed by a simple magnifying glass (convex lens) when the object is placed between the lens and its principal focus?
questions.e: When an object is placed inside the focal length of a converging lens, the lens acts as a magnifying glass, producing a virtual, upright and magnified image on the same side as the object. This is a basic property tested in optics.
questions.p: If you put object inside focal length of convex lens, e go act like magnifying glass. E go give you virtual, upright and big image for the same side.

questions.q: A biconvex lens is used to form a real image of a candle flame on a screen. The object is placed 40 cm from the lens and the sharp image forms on the screen 40 cm on the other side. What is the focal length of the lens?
questions.e: Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u with u = v = 40 cm, 1/f = 1/40 + 1/40 = 2/40, so f = 20 cm. This equal object-image distance case occurs when the object is at twice the focal length.
questions.p: If object distance and image distance both be 40 cm, e mean say object dey at 2f. So, 2f = 40 cm, which make f = 20 cm.

questions.q: A student wants to determine the refractive index of a rectangular glass slab using the real-and-apparent-depth method. A pin is viewed through the glass slab of real thickness 6 cm, and the apparent thickness measured is 4 cm. What is the refractive index of the glass?
questions.e: Refractive index equals real depth divided by apparent depth, so n = 6/4 = 1.5. This is a standard experimental method for finding the refractive index of glass.
questions.p: To find refractive index, you divide real depth by apparent depth. So, 6 divide by 4 give you 1.5.

questions.q: Two transparent media, P and Q, have refractive indices 1.2 and 1.8 respectively. A ray of light travels from medium P into medium Q, making an angle of incidence of 30° at the boundary (sin 30° = 0.5). Calculate the angle of refraction in medium Q.
questions.e: Using Snell's law, n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r): 1.2 x 0.5 = 1.8 x sin(r), so sin(r) = 0.6/1.8 = 0.333, giving r = arcsin(0.333) which is about 19.5°. The ray bends towards the normal since it enters a denser medium.
questions.p: We use Snell's law, n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r). When you calculate 1.2 times 0.5 divide by 1.8, you go get sin(r) = 0.333, so r na 19.5°.

questions.q: A compound microscope and an endoscope used in Nigerian hospitals both rely on specific optical principles. Which principle is primarily responsible for light being guided along the flexible bundle of glass fibres in an endoscope without escaping through the sides?
o: Polarization of light along the fibre axis
Total internal reflection within the fibre core
Dispersion of light into component colours
Diffraction of light at the fibre edges
questions.e: Optical fibres work by total internal reflection, where light hitting the core-cladding boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle is reflected back into the core instead of escaping. This allows light to travel along the length of the fibre with minimal loss.
questions.p: Optical fibre dey work through total internal reflection. Light dey bounce inside the core because e hit the boundary at angle wey pass critical angle.

questions.q: An object is placed 12 cm from a converging lens of focal length 18 cm. Without calculating further, what can be correctly deduced about the nature of the image formed?
o: Real, upright and diminished, formed at the focal point
Virtual, inverted and diminished, formed behind the lens
Real, inverted and magnified, formed beyond 2f
Virtual, upright and magnified, formed on the same side as the object
questions.e: Since the object distance (12 cm) is less than the focal length (18 cm), the object lies within the focal length of the converging lens, so the lens produces a virtual, upright and magnified image on the same side as the object, just like a magnifying glass.
questions.p: Because object distance 12 cm dey less than focal length 18 cm, the lens go form virtual, upright and big image. E go dey for the same side as the object.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance 5 microfarad is connected in series with another capacitor of capacitance 20 microfarad. Calculate the effective capacitance of the combination.
questions.e: For series capacitors, 1/C = 1/5 + 1/20 = 4/20 + 1/20 = 5/20, so C = 20/5 = 4 microfarad. This uses the standard product-over-sum rule for two capacitors.
questions.p: If capacitors dey series, you fit use 1/C = 1/5 + 1/20 to get 5/20. When you invert am, C go give you 4 microfarad.

questions.q: A hollow charged conducting sphere is in electrostatic equilibrium. Which of the following statements correctly describes the electric field inside the sphere and the distribution of charge on it?
o: The electric field inside is zero and all the charge resides on the outer surface
The electric field inside varies linearly with distance from the centre and charge is uniformly distributed in the volume
The electric field inside equals the field just outside the surface and charge is at the centre only
The electric field inside is maximum at the centre and charge is spread evenly throughout the volume
questions.e: For a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium, free charges redistribute until the field inside the material is zero, forcing all excess charge onto the outer surface. This is a key property used to explain electrostatic shielding.
questions.p: For conductor wey dey balance, electric field inside na zero because all the excess charge go stay for body surface. Naim make electrostatic shielding dey work.

questions.q: A student rubs a plastic ruler with a dry woollen cloth and the ruler becomes negatively charged. Which of the following best explains why this happens?
o: The ruler loses protons to the surrounding air
Protons are transferred from the woollen cloth to the ruler
Electrons are transferred from the woollen cloth to the ruler
Electrons are transferred from the ruler to the woollen cloth
questions.e: Charging by friction occurs when electrons move from one material to another; since the ruler becomes negative, it must have gained electrons from the cloth. Protons are fixed in the nucleus and are not transferred during friction.
questions.p: When you rub ruler with wool, electrons dey waka from wool enter ruler to make am negative. Proton no dey move because dem dey kampe inside nucleus.

questions.q: A 6 microfarad capacitor is charged by connecting it across a 100 V battery. The fully charged capacitor is then disconnected from the battery and connected in parallel to an identical uncharged 6 microfarad capacitor. Calculate the common potential difference across the two capacitors after connection.
questions.e: Total charge before sharing is Q = CV = 6x10⁻⁶ x 100 = 6x10⁻⁴ C, which is conserved and shared between two equal 6 microfarad capacitors in parallel, giving total capacitance 12 microfarad. Common voltage = Q/C_total = 6x10⁻⁴ / 12x10⁻⁶ = 50 V.
questions.p: Total charge wey remain constant na 6x10⁻⁴ C, and when you share am join another identical 6 microfarad capacitor, total capacitance turn 12 microfarad. Na so you go divide am to get 50 V.

questions.q: In the study of electrostatics, the term 'electric flux' through a surface is best described as
o: the force experienced by a unit positive charge placed on the surface
the work done in moving a unit charge across the surface
the capacitance of the surface per unit area
the measure of the number of electric field lines passing through the surface
questions.e: Electric flux is defined in terms of the number of field lines crossing a given surface, and it depends on the electric field strength and the orientation of the surface. It is not the same as field strength, potential, or capacitance.
questions.p: Electric flux na just how many electric field lines dey pass through surface. E no be force or capacitance at all.

questions.q: A parallel-plate capacitor with air between its plates has a capacitance of 12 microfarad. A dielectric slab of relative permittivity (dielectric constant) 3 is now inserted to completely fill the space between the plates, with the plate separation and charge unchanged. Calculate the new capacitance of the capacitor.
questions.e: Inserting a dielectric of relative permittivity 3 increases the capacitance by a factor of 3, since C = epsilon_r x C_air. So the new capacitance is 12 x 3 = 36 microfarad.
questions.p: If you put dielectric wey get relative permittivity 3 inside capacitor, capacitance go multiply by 3. So 12 x 3 go give you 36 microfarad.

questions.q: Four identical small charged spheres are arranged at the corners of a square so that each carries an equal positive charge. At the exact centre of the square, the net electric field due to the four charges is
o: equal to the field of a single charge multiplied by four
zero, because the field contributions cancel out by symmetry
maximum, because all fields add up directly
directed towards one of the corners
questions.e: By symmetry, each charge produces a field at the centre that is equal in magnitude but points away from it in a different direction, and the four vectors cancel exactly. The net field at the centre is therefore zero even though the potential there is not zero.
questions.p: As symmetry dey, dis four charges dey produce field for centre wey dey equal for magnitude but dey point opposite directions. Di four vectors cancel each other well well, so di net electric field for di centre na zero.

questions.q: A charged conducting sphere of radius 0.05 m carries a charge of 2.0 x 10⁻⁹ C in air. Using k = 9 x 10⁹ N m²/C², calculate the electric potential at the surface of the sphere.
questions.e: Potential on the surface of a charged sphere is given by V = kQ/r = (9 x 10⁹ x 2.0 x 10⁻⁹) / 0.05. This gives V = 360 V.
questions.p: To find di electric potential for di surface of sphere, you go use di formula V = kQ/r. When you put di values, V = (9 x 10⁹ x 2.0 x 10⁻⁹) / 0.05, and dat go give you 360 V.

questions.q: A parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance C is charged to a potential difference V and stores energy E. If the potential difference across the same capacitor is now doubled, what happens to the stored energy?
o: It becomes half the original energy
It becomes twice the original energy
It remains the same because capacitance is constant
It becomes four times the original energy
questions.e: Energy stored is given by E = half C V squared, so energy is proportional to the square of the voltage. Doubling the voltage increases the energy by a factor of two squared, which is four.
questions.p: Di energy wey capacitor dey store na E = half C V squared, meaning say energy dey proportional to voltage squared. If you double di voltage, di energy go multiply by two squared, wey be four times.

questions.q: In an experiment on electrostatic induction, a positively charged rod is brought near one end of an isolated neutral conductor without touching it. Which of the following correctly describes the distribution of charge on the conductor while the rod remains in place?
o: Positive charge accumulates on the end nearer the rod, negative charge on the far end
The whole conductor becomes uniformly positively charged
The whole conductor becomes uniformly negatively charged
Negative charge accumulates on the end nearer the rod, positive charge on the far end, and the conductor remains overall neutral
questions.e: Induction causes free electrons in the conductor to be attracted towards the positive rod, leaving the near end negative and the far end positive, while the total charge on the isolated conductor remains zero.
questions.p: Electrostatic induction dey make free electrons run go meet di positive rod, so negative charge go gather for near end while positive charge go stay for far end. Di conductor still remain neutral overall.

questions.q: A wire of resistance R carries a current of 2 A when a potential difference of 8 V is applied across it. What is the resistance of the wire?
questions.e: By Ohm's law, R = V/I = 8/2 = 4 ohms.
questions.p: Ohm's law talk say R = V/I. If you divide 8 V by 2 A, you go get 4 ohms.

questions.q: Four resistors, each of resistance 8 ohms, are connected in parallel. What is the effective resistance of the combination?
questions.e: For n identical resistors in parallel, effective resistance = R/n = 8/4 = 2 ohms.
questions.p: When you get n identical resistors for parallel, you just divide R by n. So, 8 divided by 4 go give you 2 ohms.

questions.q: A resistor of 5 ohms is connected in series with a parallel combination of a 6-ohm and a 3-ohm resistor. Find the total resistance of the network.
questions.e: The parallel part gives (6x3)/(6+3) = 2 ohms. Adding the series resistor gives 5 + 2 = 7 ohms.
questions.p: First, calculate the parallel part: (6x3)/(6+3) na 2 ohms. When you add the 5 ohms wey dey series, you go get 7 ohms total.

questions.q: Chidinma wants to use three identical resistors, each of 12 ohms, to obtain an effective resistance of 18 ohms. How should she connect them?
o: Connect two in series, then the combination in parallel with the third
Connect two in parallel, then the combination in series with the third
questions.e: Two 12-ohm resistors in parallel give 6 ohms; adding the third in series gives 6 + 12 = 18 ohms, which matches the required value.
questions.p: If you put two 12-ohm resistors for parallel, you go get 6 ohms. Add the third 12-ohm resistor for series, 6 plus 12 go give you 18 ohms.

questions.q: A battery of e.m.f. E and negligible internal resistance is connected to a 10-ohm resistor, producing a current of 0.6 A. If the same battery is connected to a 20-ohm resistor instead, what current will flow?
questions.e: Since internal resistance is negligible, E = IR = 0.6 x 10 = 6 V. With 20 ohms, I = E/R = 6/20 = 0.3 A.
questions.p: First, find the e.m.f. E = IR = 0.6 x 10 = 6 V. Now, use the 20-ohm resistor: I = 6/20, wey be 0.3 A.

questions.q: In the circuit shown, a 6-ohm resistor is connected in parallel with a 3-ohm resistor, and this combination is connected across a battery of e.m.f. 9 V with negligible internal resistance. What is the current supplied by the battery?
questions.e: The parallel combination gives (6x3)/(6+3) = 2 ohms. Current from battery = V/R = 9/2 = 4.5 A.
questions.p: The parallel combination of 6 ohms and 3 ohms give 2 ohms. Current na V/R, so 9 divided by 2 go give you 4.5 A.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the terminal potential difference of a battery is always less than its e.m.f. when the battery is delivering current to a circuit?
o: Part of the e.m.f. is used to overcome the internal resistance of the battery
The e.m.f. of a battery decreases permanently as soon as current flows
Some energy is lost as light in the connecting wires
Resistors in the external circuit generate their own opposing e.m.f.
questions.e: A real battery has internal resistance, so part of its e.m.f. is dropped inside it as heat (Ir), leaving a smaller terminal voltage for the external circuit.
questions.p: Battery get small internal resistance inside am. Part of the e.m.f. go waste as heat inside the battery before the current reach the outside circuit.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why electrical energy is sold to consumers in kilowatt-hours rather than in joules?
o: Electricity meters cannot be calibrated to read in joules at all
The kilowatt-hour is a smaller unit, so bills appear with smaller numbers for easy reading
The kilowatt-hour is a more convenient practical unit since domestic energy use involves large numbers of joules
The joule is too large a unit of energy to be measured by any meter
questions.e: A joule is a very small amount of energy, so household consumption would involve extremely large figures in joules. The kilowatt-hour is simply a more convenient practical unit for billing purposes.
questions.p: Joule small too much, so house consumption go carry plenty big figures. Na im make kilowatt-hour good pass for billing.

questions.q: Two identical 60 W bulbs are connected in parallel across a 240 V supply. What is the total power delivered by the supply to both bulbs?
questions.e: In a parallel connection, each bulb draws its rated power independently from the supply. The total power is simply the sum of the two bulb ratings, 60 W + 60 W = 120 W.
questions.p: For parallel connection, each bulb dey take im own power separate. Total power na just to add dem together, 60 W + 60 W = 120 W.

questions.q: A 240 V, 2 kW electric heater has its voltage reduced to 120 V while its resistance stays the same. What is the new power dissipated by the heater?
questions.e: Power is proportional to voltage squared when resistance is constant (P = V²/R). Halving the voltage reduces power by a factor of 4, so the new power is 2000/4 = 500 W.
questions.p: Power dey proportional to voltage squared when resistance no change (P = V²/R). If you reduce voltage by half, power go reduce by four, wey give 2000/4 = 500 W.

questions.q: Adaeze's family runs a 1.5 kW refrigerator continuously for 24 hours daily and a 100 W reading lamp for 5 hours daily, for a 30-day month. If electricity costs N45 per kWh, what is the total monthly bill for both appliances?
questions.e: Fridge energy = 1.5 kW x 24 h x 30 days = 1080 kWh. Lamp energy = 0.1 kW x 5 h x 30 days = 15 kWh. Total = 1095 kWh, cost = 1095 x N45 = N49,275.
questions.p: Fridge energy na 1080 kWh, lamp energy na 15 kWh, wey give total of 1095 kWh. If you multiply am by N45, you go get N49,275.

questions.q: An electric bulb is rated 220 V, 100 W. What is the resistance of the filament when the bulb is operating normally?
questions.e: Using R = V²/P, resistance equals 220 squared divided by 100, which is 48400/100 = 484 ohms.
questions.p: Make you use R = V²/P, wey be 220 squared divide by 100. E go give you 48400/100, wey come be 484 ohms.

questions.q: A certain household electricity meter records that a family consumed 250 kWh of energy in a month. Which physical quantity does this reading directly represent?
o: The peak instantaneous power drawn by the appliances
The total charge that flowed through the appliances during the month
The total electrical energy converted by the appliances during the month
The average power consumed by the appliances at any instant
questions.e: A kilowatt-hour is a unit of energy, not power or charge. The meter reading therefore represents the total electrical energy that was converted into other forms by the appliances over the month.
questions.p: Kilowatt-hour na unit for energy, no be power or charge. The meter reading show the total electrical energy wey appliances don use for the month.

questions.q: A generator supplies electrical power at a constant rate of 4000 W to a community. If the supply voltage is stepped down from 11000 V to 220 V by a transformer assumed to be 100% efficient, what is the current drawn in the low voltage secondary circuit?
questions.e: Since the transformer is ideal, power in equals power out, so current in secondary = Power/Voltage = 4000/220, which gives approximately 18.2 A.
questions.p: Because transformer dey 100% efficient, power wey enter na im equal power wey go comot. Secondary current na Power divide by Voltage, wey be 4000/220 to give 18.2 A.

questions.q: A bar magnet is dropped from rest, with its length vertical, through a horizontal coil of wire connected to a sensitive galvanometer. Which of the following best explains why a current is induced in the coil?
o: The magnet loses some of its magnetism as it falls, releasing energy as current
The magnetic flux linking the coil changes as the magnet moves, inducing an emf
The weight of the magnet is converted directly into electrical energy
The coil becomes magnetised by induction and generates its own current
questions.e: As the magnet falls through the coil, the magnetic flux through the coil changes with time. By Faraday's law, a changing flux induces an emf which drives a current.
questions.p: As the magnet dey fall enter the coil, the magnetic flux dey change with time. According to Faraday law, dis changing flux go generate emf wey dey cause current to flow.

questions.q: A solenoid of 400 turns and length 0.4 m carries a current of 2.5 A. Calculate the magnetic flux density at the centre of the solenoid. [Take permeability of free space, mu_0 = 4pi x 10⁻⁷ H/m]
questions.e: B = mu_0n × I, where n = N/L = 400/0.4 = 1000 turns per metre. So B = 4pi x 10⁻⁷ x 1000 x 2.5 = 3.14 x 10⁻³ T.
questions.p: We use the formula B = mu_0n × I, where n na the number of turns per metre wey be 1000. When we multiply everything, we go get 3.14 x 10⁻³ T.

questions.q: Chidinma wants to increase the strength of an electromagnet made from a solenoid wound on a soft iron core without changing the core or the number of turns. Which single action below will achieve this?
o: Stretch the coil so the turns are more spaced out
Reduce the current flowing through the solenoid
Replace the soft iron core with an air core
Increase the current flowing through the solenoid
questions.e: The strength of an electromagnet increases with current, since the magnetic field produced is proportional to the current flowing through the coil. Reducing current, spacing turns out, or removing the iron core would all weaken it.
questions.p: To make electromagnet strong, you suppose increase the current wey dey flow inside the coil. If you reduce am or remove iron core, the strength go reduce.

questions.q: A rectangular coil of area 0.02 m² is placed with its plane parallel to a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T. What is the magnetic flux linking the coil in this position?
questions.e: Flux = B × A × cos(theta), where theta is the angle between the field and the normal to the coil. When the plane is parallel to the field, the normal is perpendicular to the field, so theta = 90° and cos(90°) = 0, giving zero flux.
questions.p: Magnetic flux na B × A × cos(theta). Since the plane of the coil dey parallel to the field, the angle theta na 90°, and cos(90°) na zero, so the flux be zero.

questions.q: A rod PQ is free to rotate about end P in a horizontal plane under a uniform vertical magnetic field. An emf is induced between P and Q only when the rod is:
o: placed in a region where the field is zero
aligned parallel to the magnetic field lines
rotating about P so that Q sweeps through the field
questions.e: An emf is induced only when there is relative motion between the conductor and the field, cutting field lines. A rotating rod sweeps across the field lines, continuously changing the flux and inducing an emf; a stationary rod does not.
questions.p: Ems go only dey induced if the conductor dey cut magnetic field lines. When the rod dey rotate about P, Q dey sweep through the field to generate emf.

questions.q: A metal disc is rotated rapidly between the poles of a strong magnet, with its plane perpendicular to the field, while its edge and centre are connected through a stationary circuit to a galvanometer. This arrangement demonstrates the principle behind which device?
o: The eddy current brake / disc dynamo
questions.e: A rotating conducting disc cutting magnetic field lines generates induced currents (eddy currents) that flow radially, which is the working principle of devices such as the disc dynamo and eddy current brakes. This differs from a generator, which uses a coil, not a solid disc.
questions.p: As the metal disc dey spin inside the magnet field, it dey produce eddy currents. Na dis same principle dem dey use for eddy current brake and disc dynamo.

questions.q: Two long straight parallel wires carry currents in the same direction. What is the nature of the force between them, and why does it occur?
o: Zero, because parallel wires never interact magnetically
Attractive, because each wire's magnetic field exerts a force on the other current-carrying wire
Repulsive, because the magnetic fields between them cancel out completely
Repulsive, because like currents repel each other
questions.e: Each current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field that exerts a force on the other wire carrying current. When the currents flow in the same direction, the force between the wires is attractive.
questions.p: The two wires dey attract each other because each wire get magnetic field wey dey push the other current-carrying wire. When current dey flow same direction, the force na attraction.

questions.q: A body of mass 0.5 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency 4 rad/s and amplitude 0.2 m. What is the maximum kinetic energy of the body during the motion?
questions.e: Maximum KE equals total energy = 1/2m × w² × A² = 0.5 × 0.5 × 16 × 0.04 = 0.16 J. This occurs when the body passes through the equilibrium (mean) position where speed is maximum.
questions.p: Maximum kinetic energy na 1/2m × w² × A². If you calculate 0.5 × 0.5 × 16 × 0.04, you go get 0.16 J. Dis one dey happen for di mean position where speed dey maximum.

questions.q: In a simple pendulum undergoing small oscillations, which of the following correctly describes the energy changes between the extreme position and the mean (equilibrium) position?
o: Kinetic energy is maximum at the extreme position and zero at the mean position
Potential energy is maximum at the extreme position and minimum at the mean position
Total mechanical energy is zero at the mean position and maximum at the extreme position
Kinetic and potential energy are both maximum at the mean position
questions.e: At the extreme position the pendulum momentarily stops, so all the energy is potential (maximum), while at the mean position all the energy is kinetic (potential energy minimum). Total mechanical energy stays constant throughout.
questions.p: For extreme position, di pendulum stop small, so all energy na potential energy. For mean position, di potential energy dey minimum and kinetic energy dey maximum. Total energy no dey change.

questions.q: Two simple pendulums, P and Q, have lengths in the ratio 1:4. If pendulum P has a period of 1.5 s, what is the period of pendulum Q?
questions.e: Since T is proportional to √L, doubling the ratio of lengths by 4 means the period increases by √4 = 2. So Q's period = 1.5 × 2 = 3.0 s.
questions.p: Period T dey proportional to square root of length L. Since length ratio na 1:4, period go increase by square root of 4, wey be 2. So 1.5 s times 2 give us 3.0 s.

questions.q: A particle moves with simple harmonic motion described by x = 5 cos(2t), where x is in centimetres and t is in seconds. What is the maximum acceleration of the particle?
questions.e: Maximum acceleration equals w² × A, where w = 2 rad/s and A = 5 cm. So maximum acceleration = 4 × 5 = 20 cm/s².
questions.p: Maximum acceleration na w² × A. If w na 2 rad/s and A na 5 cm, den 2 squared times 5 go give you 20 cm/s². Na simple calculation be dat.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a necessary condition for a system to undergo simple harmonic motion?
o: The restoring force must be directed towards a fixed equilibrium point
The restoring force must be directly proportional to the displacement from equilibrium
The amplitude of oscillation must be the same as the length of the oscillating system
The acceleration must always be directed opposite to the displacement
questions.e: Simple harmonic motion requires a restoring force proportional to displacement and directed towards equilibrium, with acceleration opposite to displacement. There is no requirement that amplitude equals the length of the system, so this is not a necessary condition.
questions.p: Simple harmonic motion need restoring force wey dey proportional to displacement and dey point to equilibrium. Amplitude no get any condition to be equal to length of system. So dat one no correct.

questions.q: A nucleus of radium-226 (atomic number 88) decays by emitting an alpha particle. What is the resulting daughter nucleus?
questions.e: An alpha particle has mass number 4 and atomic number 2, so it is removed from the parent nucleus. This gives mass number 226-4=222 and atomic number 88-2=86, which is radon.
questions.p: Alpha particle get mass number 4 and atomic number 2. If you remove am from radium, you go get mass number 222 and atomic number 86, wey be radon.

questions.q: Which property is the same for all isotopes of a given element?
o: Number of protons in the nucleus
Number of neutrons in the nucleus
questions.e: Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons (atomic number) but different numbers of neutrons, so their mass numbers differ. The proton number defines the element.
questions.p: Isotopes of one element get the same number of protons, wey be the atomic number. Na the proton number dey decide which element e be, even if the neutron number dey different.

questions.q: A Geiger counter placed near a radioactive source in a Zaria physics laboratory records a count rate of 960 counts per minute. After 3 half-lives have passed, what count rate would be expected, assuming the background count is negligible?
questions.e: After each half-life the activity halves. After 3 half-lives the activity becomes 960 divided by 2³ = 960/8 = 120 counts per minute.
questions.p: Every half-life, the activity dey divide by two. Since three half-lives don pass, you go divide 960 by 8, wey give you 120 counts per minute.

questions.q: The number of undecayed nuclei in a radioactive sample reduces from 5.0 x 10¹⁸ to 1.25 x 10¹⁸ after 24 years. What is the half-life of the sample?
questions.e: The ratio 5.0/1.25 = 4 = 2², meaning 2 half-lives occurred in 24 years. So one half-life is 24/2 = 12 years.
questions.p: If you divide 5.0 by 1.25, you go get 4, wey be 2 power 2. This mean say two half-lives don pass for 24 years, so one half-life na 12 years.

questions.q: A radioactive sample has a decay constant of 2.0 x 10⁻³ per second. What is the activity of the sample when it contains 3.0 x 10⁸ undecayed atoms?
questions.e: Activity A equals decay constant multiplied by number of atoms, so A = 2.0x10⁻³ x 3.0x10⁸ = 6.0x10⁵ disintegrations per second.
questions.p: Activity na decay constant times the number of atoms. If you multiply 2.0x10⁻³ by 3.0x10⁸, you go get 6.0x10⁵ disintegrations per second.

questions.q: A radioactive source used for sterilizing medical equipment in a Benin hospital has a half-life of 15 years. A new sample contains 2.0 x 10²² atoms. Calculate, to 2 significant figures, how many atoms remain undecayed after 45 years.
questions.e: 45 years is exactly 3 half-lives (45/15=3), so the number remaining is 2.0x10²² divided by 2³ = 2.0x10²²/8 = 2.5x10²¹ atoms.
questions.p: 45 years na three half-lives because 45 divide by 15 na 3. You go divide 2.0x10²² by 8, and that one go give you 2.5x10²¹ atoms.

questions.q: A hospital stores a radioisotope whose decay constant is 0.0231 per day (ln 2 = 0.693). If the sample initially has 1000 g, approximately how many days are needed for the mass to reduce to 125 g?
questions.e: Half-life = ln2/decay constant = 0.693/0.0231 = 30 days. Reducing from 1000 g to 125 g needs a factor of 8, which is 2³, so 3 half-lives: 3 x 30 = 90 days.
questions.p: Half-life na 0.693 divide by 0.0231, wey be 30 days. To go from 1000g to 125g, you need three half-lives, so 3 times 30 na 90 days.

questions.q: A student in a Lagos physics laboratory shines ultraviolet light on a clean zinc plate and observes that electrons are emitted instantly, even when the light intensity is very low. Which property of light best explains this instant emission?
o: Light has a very high speed of propagation in vacuum
Light energy is carried in discrete packets (photons) that are absorbed one at a time by electrons
Light behaves as a continuous wave that gradually heats the surface
Light intensity determines the energy of each individual photon
questions.e: Photoelectric emission is instantaneous because each photon delivers its energy in one quantum to a single electron, unlike the wave model which predicts a time delay for energy to build up. Intensity only affects the number of photons, not their individual energy.
questions.p: Na photon energy wey electron dey take one-one time make light take emit electron sharp-sharp. Intensity naim just dey show how many photon dey, e no mean say photon energy go increase.

questions.q: In a photoelectric experiment, a graph of stopping potential (Vs) against frequency (f) of incident light is a straight line that does not pass through the origin. What does the slope of this graph represent?
o: The work function of the metal divided by electronic charge
The threshold frequency of the metal
Planck's constant divided by electronic charge (h/e)
questions.e: From eVs = hf - W0, we get Vs = (h/e)f - W0/e, which is a straight line whose slope is h/e. The intercept on the frequency axis gives the threshold frequency, not the slope.
questions.p: If you check di equation $eV_s = hf - W_0$, as you plot $V_s$ against $f$, di slope na $h/e$. Na so di formula arrange am, abi?

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes what happens to the photoelectric current when the intensity of monochromatic light incident on a photosensitive surface is increased, while the frequency is kept constant and above the threshold frequency?
o: The maximum kinetic energy of the electrons increases proportionally
The threshold frequency of the metal decreases
The photoelectric current increases because more photons strike the surface per second
The stopping potential increases because electrons gain more energy
questions.e: Increasing intensity at a fixed frequency increases the number of photons hitting the surface per second, releasing more electrons and raising the current. The energy of each photon, and hence the maximum kinetic energy and stopping potential, depends only on frequency, not intensity.
questions.p: If you increase intensity, more photon go hit di surface, and more electrons go comot, so current go increase. Na frequency dey control di energy and stopping potential, no be intensity.

questions.q: Which of the following observations in the photoelectric effect could NOT be explained by the classical wave theory of light, and led Einstein to propose the photon concept?
o: Increasing the intensity of light increases the number of photoelectrons emitted
Photoelectrons are emitted only when the frequency of light exceeds a certain threshold value, regardless of intensity
Light exhibits interference and diffraction patterns in Young's double slit experiment
Light can be reflected and refracted at a boundary between two media
questions.e: Classical wave theory predicted that emission should occur at any frequency given enough time or intensity, but experiments showed emission depends on frequency exceeding a threshold value instantly. This could only be explained by treating light as photons with discrete energy hf.
questions.p: Classical wave theory bin think say light fit emit electron for any frequency if time dey. But experiment show say na only when frequency pass threshold value light go fit emit electron. Na Einstein photon theory explain say light dey come as discrete packet of energy hf.

questions.q: A metal surface with work function 2.2 eV is illuminated by light of wavelength 400 nm. Given h = 6.63 x 10⁻³⁴ Js, c = 3.0 x 10⁸ m/s and 1 eV = 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹ J, calculate the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons in eV.
questions.e: Photon energy = hc/lambda = (6.63e-34 x 3.0e8)/(400e-9) = 4.97 x 10⁻¹⁹ J = 3.107 eV. Maximum KE = photon energy minus work function = 3.107 - 2.2 = 0.907 eV.
questions.p: First, we calculate photon energy as hc/lambda, wey give us 3.107 eV. To get maximum kinetic energy, we subtract work function 2.2 eV from 3.107 eV. The final answer come be 0.907 eV.

questions.q: Blue light and red light of the same intensity are separately incident on a clean sodium plate, and both cause photoelectric emission. Which of the following statements correctly compares the photoelectrons produced?
o: Photoelectrons produced by blue light have greater maximum kinetic energy than those produced by red light
Photoelectrons produced by red light have greater maximum kinetic energy than those produced by blue light
Both sets of photoelectrons have the same maximum kinetic energy since the intensities are equal
The number of photoelectrons emitted depends only on the frequency of the light, not the intensity
questions.e: Blue light has a higher frequency than red light, so each photon of blue light carries more energy. Since maximum kinetic energy depends on frequency through hf - W0, blue light produces photoelectrons with greater kinetic energy.
questions.p: Blue light get higher frequency pass red light, so e get more energy per photon. Since maximum kinetic energy depend on frequency, blue light go produce electron wey get more kinetic energy pass red light.

questions.q: In the context of energy quantisation, what does the term 'quantum of energy' mean as proposed by Max Planck?
o: The smallest discrete packet of energy that can be absorbed or emitted by matter, equal to hf
The amount of energy required to remove an electron completely from a metal surface
The total energy possessed by an electron in its lowest orbit around the nucleus
The continuous flow of energy that can take on any value without restriction
questions.e: Planck proposed that energy is not emitted or absorbed continuously but in discrete packets called quanta, each with energy E = hf. This idea of quantisation was central to resolving issues like blackbody radiation and the photoelectric effect.
questions.p: Planck talk say energy no dey flow like water, e dey come in small-small packet wey we dey call quanta. Each packet get energy E = hf. This one na the main way to understand how energy dey behave for atomic level.

questions.q: Newton's law of universal gravitation states that the force between two point masses is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. If the distance between two masses is tripled, the gravitational force between them becomes
questions.e: Gravitational force follows F proportional to 1/r². Tripling r makes the force 1/3² = 1/9 of the original value.
questions.p: Gravitational force dey follow inverse square law with distance. If you multiply the distance by 3, the force go come down by 3², wey be 1/9 of the original force.

questions.q: A satellite orbits the Earth close to its surface, where the acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/s² and the radius of the Earth is 6.4 x 10⁶ m. Calculate the orbital speed of the satellite.
questions.e: For a satellite near the surface, gravity supplies centripetal force: v = √gR = √(10 x 6.4 x 10⁶) = √(6.4 x 10⁷) approximately 8000 m/s.
questions.p: For satellite wey dey near ground, na gravity dey provide centripetal force. When you use formula v = √gR, you go get √(10 x 6.4 x 10⁶), wey give you 8.0 x 10³ m/s.

questions.q: Which statement correctly expresses Kepler's second law of planetary motion?
o: The orbital speed of a planet is the same at all points in its orbit
The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the mean distance from the sun
A line joining a planet to the sun sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time
All planets move in circular orbits with the sun at the centre
questions.e: Kepler's second law, the law of areas, states that the radius vector from the sun to a planet sweeps equal areas in equal times, meaning planets move faster when nearer the sun.
questions.p: Kepler second law talk say line wey join planet to sun dey sweep equal areas for equal time. E mean say planet dey move fast when e near sun.

questions.q: A geostationary satellite is one that
o: has an orbital period equal to the Earth's period of rotation and appears fixed above a point on the equator
falls freely towards the Earth without any orbital motion
orbits the Earth once every 90 minutes at low altitude
moves in a polar orbit scanning the whole Earth once daily
questions.e: A geostationary satellite orbits in the equatorial plane with a period of 24 hours, matching Earth's rotation, so it stays above the same point on the equator.
questions.p: Geostationary satellite period na 24 hours just like Earth rotation. E dey stay fixed for one place for top equator so people fit see am well.

questions.q: At what altitude above the Earth's surface would a satellite's weight be reduced to one-quarter of its weight at the surface? Take the radius of the Earth as 6400 km.
questions.e: Weight follows inverse square law with distance from Earth's centre, so (R/(R+h))² = 1/4 gives (R+h) = 2R, meaning h = R = 6400 km.
questions.p: Since weight follow inverse square law, for weight to reduce to one-quarter, distance from centre must double. E mean say altitude h must be equal to Earth radius R, wey be 6400 km.

questions.q: A communication satellite of mass 500 kg is in a stable circular orbit around the Earth. Which of the following correctly describes the energy changes if the satellite moves to a higher orbit?
o: Both kinetic energy and potential energy increase
Kinetic energy decreases while potential energy increases
Kinetic energy increases while potential energy decreases
Both kinetic energy and potential energy decrease
questions.e: At a higher orbit the orbital speed is smaller since v = √(GM/r) decreases with r, so kinetic energy falls, while gravitational potential energy increases as the satellite moves farther from Earth.
questions.p: If satellite go higher orbit, speed go reduce, so kinetic energy go decrease. But because e dey far from Earth, potential energy go increase.

questions.q: The gravitational field strength at a point above the Earth's surface is 4.0 N/kg. If the mass of the Earth is 6.0 x 10²⁴ kg, calculate the distance of the point from the centre of the Earth. (G = 6.67 x 10⁻¹¹ Nm²/kg²)
questions.e: Using g = GM/r², r = √(GM/g) = √(6.67e-11 x 6.0e24 / 4.0) which gives about 1.0 x 10⁷ m. This comes directly from rearranging the gravitational field formula.
questions.p: Make you use g = GM/r² to find distance r. When you put the numbers inside, you go get 1.0 x 10⁷ m.

questions.q: Two point masses are separated by a distance d and exert a gravitational force F on each other. If the distance between them is reduced to d/3, what is the new force in terms of F?
questions.e: Gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, so reducing the distance to one-third increases the force by a factor of 3² = 9. This gives a new force of 9F.
questions.p: Gravity force dey opposite to distance square. If distance come reduce to d/3, the force go multiply by 3², wey be 9F.

questions.q: A student in Kano observes that a planet orbiting the Sun has an orbital period of 8 years. According to Kepler's third law, if Earth's orbital radius is taken as 1 astronomical unit (AU) and its period as 1 year, what is the orbital radius of the planet in AU?
questions.e: Kepler's third law states T² is proportional to r³, so r = T^(2/3). Taking T = 8 years gives r = 8^(2/3) = 4 AU.
questions.p: As Kepler law talk say T² dey equal to r³, na im make r = T^(2/3). If you put T = 8 years, you go get 4 AU.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why astronauts in an orbiting space station experience apparent weightlessness, even though Earth's gravity still acts on them?
o: The space station is completely outside Earth's gravitational field
The astronauts and the station are both in continuous free fall around the Earth
Gravity does not exist in space
The station's engines cancel out the pull of gravity
questions.e: In orbit, gravity provides the centripetal force needed to keep the station and astronauts falling continuously towards Earth along a curved path, so they feel weightless even though gravity is still acting. This is not the absence of gravity, just continuous free fall.
questions.p: Astronauts dey feel weightlessness because both them and the space station dey do free fall together round Earth, no be say gravity no dey.

questions.q: The weight of an object on the surface of the Earth is 600 N. If the object is taken to a height equal to the Earth's radius above the surface, what will its new weight be?
questions.e: At a height equal to the Earth's radius R, the distance from the centre becomes 2R, so gravitational force falls by a factor of 2² = 4. The new weight is 600/4 = 150 N.
questions.p: If distance from centre become 2R because of height, gravity go reduce by 2², wey be 4. So you divide 600 N by 4 to get 150 N.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is a correct consequence of Kepler's first law of planetary motion?
o: A planet's orbit is an ellipse with the Sun at one of the two foci
The square of a planet's period is proportional to the cube of its orbital radius
All planets move in perfect circles with the Sun at the centre
Planets move faster when they are closer to the Sun and slower when farther away
questions.e: Kepler's first law states that planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun located at one focus, not at the centre. The other statements describe Kepler's second and third laws instead.
questions.p: Kepler first law talk say planet path na ellipse, and Sun dey one of the two foci. E no talk say circle.

questions.q: A planet of mass m orbits a star of mass M in a circular orbit of radius r. Given that G is the universal gravitational constant, derive an expression for the orbital speed v of the planet in terms of G, M and r.
questions.e: For a circular orbit, gravitational force supplies the centripetal force: GMm/r² = mv²/r. Solving for v gives v = √(GM/r), which is the correct orbital speed formula.
questions.p: Make you equalize gravitational force and centripetal force, na im be GMm/r² = mv²/r. When you solve am, v = √(GM/r) go come out.

questions.q: An alternating current is represented by i = 5 sin(100pi × t) amperes. What is the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) value of the current?
questions.e: The r.m.s value equals the peak value divided by √2. So r.m.s = 5/√2 = 3.54 A.
questions.p: To find r.m.s, na peak value divide by √2. So r.m.s = 5/√2 = 3.54 A.

questions.q: A pure inductor of inductance 0.2 H is connected to an a.c. source of frequency 50 Hz. Calculate the inductive reactance of the inductor. (Take π = 3.142)
questions.e: Inductive reactance X_L = 2pi × f × L = 2 x 3.142 x 50 x 0.2 = 62.8 ohms. This is the opposition offered by an inductor to alternating current.
questions.p: Inductive reactance formula na X_L = 2pi × f × L. If you multiply 2 x 3.142 x 50 x 0.2, you go get 62.8 ohms.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance 50 microfarads is connected to an a.c. supply of frequency 60 Hz. Determine the capacitive reactance of the capacitor. (Take π = 3.142)
questions.e: Capacitive reactance X_C = 1/(2pi × f × C) = 1/(2 x 3.142 x 60 x 50x10⁻⁶) = 53.1 ohms. Note that X_C decreases as frequency or capacitance increases.
questions.p: Capacitive reactance na X_C = 1/(2pi × f × C). When you calculate am with 50 microfarads and 60 Hz, e go give you 53.1 ohms.

questions.q: In an a.c. circuit, which of the following statements correctly describes the phase relationship between current and voltage in a circuit containing only a pure capacitor?
o: Current and voltage are in phase
questions.e: In a purely capacitive circuit, the current reaches its peak value a quarter cycle before the voltage, so current leads voltage by 90 degrees. This is the opposite of what happens in a purely inductive circuit.
questions.p: For pure capacitor circuit, current dey run ahead of voltage. E dey lead voltage by 90 degrees.

questions.q: A series circuit consists of a resistor of resistance 30 ohms connected in series with an inductor whose reactance is 40 ohms, across an a.c. source. Calculate the impedance of the circuit.
questions.e: For a series R-L circuit, impedance Z = √(R² + X_L²) = √(30² + 40²) = √2500 = 50 ohms. The resistance and reactance combine as perpendicular vectors, not by simple addition.
questions.p: Z = √(R² + X_L²) for series R-L circuit. If you put 30 ohms and 40 ohms inside, impedance go be 50 ohms.

questions.q: A series L-C-R circuit is at resonance when connected to an a.c. source. Which of the following statements about the circuit at resonance is correct?
o: The impedance is at its maximum value and equals the resistance
The inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance and the impedance is minimum
The current in the circuit is zero
The capacitive reactance is greater than the inductive reactance
questions.e: At resonance, X_L equals X_C so they cancel out, leaving the impedance equal to only the resistance, which is its minimum possible value. This causes the current in the circuit to be maximum at resonance.
questions.p: For resonance, inductive reactance and capacitive reactance balance out. Impedance come dey at minimum value wey equal to resistance.

questions.q: An a.c. generator produces a voltage given by v = 311 sin(314t) volts. What is the root-mean-square value of the voltage, correct to the nearest volt?
questions.e: The r.m.s. value of a sinusoidal voltage is the peak value divided by √2. So Vrms = 311/√2 ≈ 220 V, which is the standard mains voltage in Nigeria.
questions.p: To find r.m.s. voltage, you divide peak voltage by √2. So 311 divide by √2 go give you 220 V, wey be the standard light voltage for Naija.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the condition of a series L-C-R circuit at resonance?
o: The impedance is maximum and the current is minimum
The current leads the voltage by 90 degrees
The impedance is minimum and equal to the resistance, and current is maximum
The inductive reactance is zero while the capacitive reactance is maximum
questions.e: At resonance, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance so they cancel out, leaving only resistance to oppose current flow. This makes the impedance a minimum (equal to R) and the current a maximum, in phase with the voltage.
questions.p: When resonance happen for L-C-R circuit, inductive reactance and capacitive reactance cancel each other. Na only resistance remain, so impedance go small reach minimum while current go climb reach maximum.

questions.q: A student connects a pure resistor of 25 ohms to an a.c. source and records an r.m.s. current of 4 A. What is the average power dissipated in the resistor?
questions.e: For a resistor, average power equals Irms² multiplied by R. So power = 4² x 25 = 400 W, since r.m.s. values are used directly for power calculations in a.c. circuits.
questions.p: For resistor, average power na Irms² multiply by R. So if you do 4² multiply by 25, you go get 400 W straight.

questions.q: A capacitor of unknown capacitance is connected to a 50 Hz a.c. mains supply and draws a current such that its reactance is 265.4 ohms. If the applied r.m.s. voltage is 220 V, calculate the r.m.s. current flowing through the capacitor, correct to two decimal places.
questions.e: By analogy with Ohm's law for a.c. circuits, current equals voltage divided by reactance. So I = 220/265.4 ≈ 0.83 A.
questions.p: You fit use Ohm's law find current by dividing voltage with reactance. When you divide 220 by 265.4, you go get 0.83 A.

questions.q: In a certain a.c. circuit containing only an inductor, which statement correctly describes the relationship between the current and the applied voltage?
o: Current and voltage are in phase
questions.e: In a purely inductive a.c. circuit, the back e.m.f. generated by the inductor causes the current to lag behind the applied voltage by a quarter cycle. This means the voltage leads the current by 90 degrees.
questions.p: For circuit wey get only inductor, current dey delay behind voltage because of back e.m.f. E come mean say voltage dey lead current by 90 degrees.

questions.q: The current in an a.c. circuit varies with time as i = 10 sin(200pi × t) amperes. If this current flows through a resistor of 15 ohms for a long time, what is the average (mean) power dissipated in the resistor?
questions.e: The peak current is 10 A, so the r.m.s. current is 10/√2 A. Average power equals Irms² x R = (10/√2)² x 15 = 50 x 15 = 750 W.
questions.p: First find r.m.s. current by dividing peak current 10 by √2. Then use am calculate power as Irms² multiply by R, wey give you 750 W.

questions.q: A semiconductor material is one whose electrical conductivity lies between that of a conductor and an insulator. Which of these is the most important semiconductor element used in making diodes and transistors?
questions.e: Silicon is the most widely used semiconductor material because of its ideal energy gap and abundance. Copper is a conductor while sulphur and mica are insulators.
questions.p: Silicon na the main material wey dem dey use make semiconductor because e get better energy gap and e plenty for ground. Copper na conductor, while sulphur and mica na insulator.

questions.q: In a pure (intrinsic) semiconductor, adding a small amount of a pentavalent impurity such as phosphorus produces a material with an excess of free electrons. This type of doped semiconductor is called a(n):
questions.e: Pentavalent atoms donate extra free electrons, making electrons the majority charge carriers, so the material becomes n-type. p-type is formed instead by trivalent (hole-donating) impurities.
questions.p: Pentavalent atoms dey give extra free electrons make electrons plenty pass, naim make am become n-type semiconductor. Na trivalent impurities dey form p-type.

questions.q: A p-n junction diode is said to be forward biased when:
o: the p-side is connected to the negative terminal and n-side to the positive terminal of the battery
the p-side is connected to the positive terminal and n-side to the negative terminal of the battery
both sides are connected to the same terminal of the battery
no battery is connected to the junction
questions.e: Forward bias occurs when the positive terminal is joined to the p-side and the negative terminal to the n-side, narrowing the depletion layer and allowing current to flow easily. The reverse connection widens the depletion region and blocks current.
questions.p: Forward bias dey happen when you join positive terminal to p-side and negative terminal to n-side, make current fit flow well. If you reverse am, current no go fit pass.

questions.q: A full-wave bridge rectifier made of four diodes is connected to an alternating supply of peak voltage 20 V. Ignoring the voltage drop across the diodes, what is the peak output voltage across the load?
questions.e: A bridge rectifier converts both halves of the AC cycle into output pulses without reducing the peak value, so the output peak voltage equals the input peak voltage of 20 V. Only the shape (always positive) changes, not the magnitude.
questions.p: Bridge rectifier dey convert both sides of AC cycle make output peak voltage remain the same 20 V. Na only the shape wey dey always positive dey change, not the value.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a half-wave rectifier is less efficient than a full-wave rectifier for converting AC to DC?
o: It uses only one diode to conduct during both halves of the input cycle
It blocks one half of the input cycle, so current flows for only half the time
It requires four diodes arranged in a bridge network
It produces a perfectly smooth DC output without a capacitor
questions.e: A half-wave rectifier allows current to flow during only one half-cycle of the AC input and blocks the other half, so it wastes half the available power. Full-wave rectifiers use both halves of the cycle, making them more efficient.
questions.p: Half-wave rectifier dey allow current to flow for only one half of AC input and block the other half, naim make am waste power. Full-wave rectifier dey use both halves, so e dey efficient pass.

questions.q: A transistor is connected in the common-emitter mode. If the base current is 0.04 mA and the collector current is 4.0 mA, calculate the current amplification factor (beta) of the transistor.
questions.e: Beta equals collector current divided by base current, which is 4.0 mA divided by 0.04 mA, giving 100. This shows the transistor strongly amplifies the small base current into a larger collector current.
questions.p: Beta na collector current divide by base current, wey be 4.0 mA divide by 0.04 mA to give 100. Dis one show say transistor dey turn small base current to big collector current.

questions.q: In an NPN transistor used as a switch in common-emitter configuration, a small change in base current of 20 microamperes produces a change in collector current of 2.0 mA. If the base current is further increased by 50 microamperes, calculate the additional change in collector current, assuming the same current gain applies.
questions.e: The current gain is 2.0 mA divided by 20 microamperes, which equals 100. Multiplying this gain by the new base current change of 50 microamperes gives an additional collector current change of 5.0 mA.
questions.p: Current gain na 2.0 mA divide by 20 microamperes, wey give 100. When you multiply this gain by the new base current change of 50 microamperes, you go get 5.0 mA collector current.

questions.q: A student connects a silicon diode, an AC source, a resistor and a capacitor to build a simple power supply circuit. The capacitor is placed in parallel with the load resistor after the diode. What is the main function of this capacitor in the circuit?
o: To increase the frequency of the rectified output
To prevent any current from flowing through the load resistor
To smoothen the rectified output by reducing the ripples
To change the AC supply into a higher voltage before rectification
questions.e: The capacitor charges up during peaks of the rectified voltage and discharges slowly through the load when the voltage falls, filling in the gaps and smoothing the pulsating DC into a steadier output. It does not change frequency, boost voltage, or block current to the load.
questions.p: The capacitor dey charge when voltage high and discharge slowly when voltage drop, to remove ripples and make DC output smooth. E no dey increase frequency or block current.

questions.q: A p-type semiconductor is formed when pure (intrinsic) silicon is doped with a trivalent impurity such as boron. What is the effect of this doping?
o: It creates holes which act as majority charge carriers
It converts the silicon into a perfect conductor
It removes all free electrons from the silicon lattice
It creates extra free electrons that increase conductivity
questions.e: Boron has only three valence electrons, so when it bonds with silicon one bond is left incomplete, creating a hole. These holes become the majority charge carriers in a p-type material.
questions.p: Boron get three valence electrons, so when e bond with silicon, e dey create hole. Na dis holes dey serve as majority charge carriers for p-type material.

questions.q: In a zener diode used as a voltage regulator, the diode is deliberately connected in:
o: Forward bias, so that it conducts like an ordinary diode
Forward bias, with the cathode connected to the positive terminal
Series with an inductor only, without any resistor
Reverse bias, operating in its breakdown region at a fixed voltage
questions.e: A zener diode regulates voltage by operating in reverse bias at its breakdown (zener) voltage, where the voltage across it stays nearly constant despite changes in current. This is different from normal diode forward operation.
questions.p: Zener diode dey regulate voltage as e dey work for reverse bias for im breakdown region. E dey make voltage stay constant even if current change.

questions.q: A transistor is connected in the common-base configuration. If the emitter current is 8.0 mA and the current gain (alpha) of the transistor is 0.96, calculate the collector current.
questions.e: In common-base mode, collector current equals alpha multiplied by emitter current. So Ic = 0.96 x 8.0 mA = 7.68 mA.
questions.p: For common-base mode, collector current na alpha times emitter current. If we multiply 0.96 by 8.0 mA, we go get 7.68 mA.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the depletion region of an unbiased p-n junction diode?
o: It expands to zero width once the diode is manufactured
It is a region rich in free electrons from the n-side only
It is the region where forward current flows most easily
It is a narrow region near the junction with no mobile charge carriers, containing fixed ions
questions.e: At the junction, electrons and holes diffuse across and recombine, leaving behind fixed positive and negative ions on either side. This creates a narrow depletion region with no free charge carriers, which opposes further diffusion until biased.
questions.p: For the junction, electrons and holes dey combine, leave fixed ions wey no get mobile charge carriers. Na dis small place we dey call depletion region.

questions.q: A transistor amplifier in common-emitter mode has an input resistance of 500 ohms and produces a voltage gain of 120. If a small AC signal of peak value 4 mV is applied to the base, calculate the peak output voltage.
questions.e: Voltage gain is output voltage divided by input voltage, so output voltage = gain x input voltage = 120 x 0.004 V = 0.48 V. The input resistance value is not needed for this calculation.
questions.p: Voltage gain na output voltage divide by input voltage, so output voltage na gain times input voltage. When we multiply 120 by 0.004 V, we get 0.48 V.

questions.q: Chidinma wants to design a circuit that converts an alternating current from a 50 Hz mains supply into a smoother pulsating direct current using the fewest number of diodes, while still rectifying both halves of the wave using a transformer with a centre-tapped secondary coil. How many diodes does this type of full-wave rectifier circuit require?
questions.e: A full-wave rectifier using a centre-tapped transformer needs only two diodes, since each diode conducts during alternate half-cycles using the two ends of the centre-tapped secondary coil. This is different from the bridge rectifier, which needs four diodes but no centre tap.
questions.p: Full-wave rectifier wey use centre-tapped transformer need only two diodes. Each diode dey carry current for alternate half-cycles.

questions.q: The output frequency of the ripple voltage from a full-wave rectifier connected to a 50 Hz AC mains supply is:
questions.e: A full-wave rectifier produces one output pulse for every half-cycle of the input, so the ripple frequency is twice the supply frequency. Therefore the ripple frequency is 2 x 50 Hz = 100 Hz.
questions.p: Full-wave rectifier dey produce two pulses for every one cycle, so ripple frequency na twice the supply frequency. 2 times 50 Hz give us 100 Hz.

questions.q: In a certain NPN transistor circuit operating in the active region, the emitter current is found to be 5.2 mA while the base current is 0.2 mA. Determine the current gain (beta) of the transistor in common-emitter mode.
questions.e: Since Ie = Ib + Ic, the collector current is Ic = 5.2 - 0.2 = 5.0 mA. Beta is Ic divided by Ib, so beta = 5.0 / 0.2 = 25.
questions.p: Collector current na emitter current minus base current, which be 5.0 mA. Beta na collector current divide by base current, so 5.0 divide by 0.2 give us 25.

questions.q: Which property of a fluid is responsible for the formation of a spherical shape by a small raindrop falling freely in air?
questions.e: Surface tension causes the liquid surface to behave like a stretched elastic skin, minimising surface area, which gives a sphere for a given volume. Viscosity resists flow but does not cause this shape.
questions.p: Na surface tension dey make water drop form round shape like ball because e dey make the liquid surface tight like rubber. E dey reduce surface area make the volume remain constant.

questions.q: Water flows steadily through a horizontal pipe that narrows from a wide section of cross-sectional area 8 cm² to a narrow section of area 2 cm². If the speed of water in the wide section is 0.5 m/s, what is the speed in the narrow section?
questions.e: By the equation of continuity, A1v1 = A2v2, so v2 = (8x0.5)/2 = 2.0 m/s. The narrower section must have a higher speed to keep the volume flow rate constant.
questions.p: We go use equation of continuity A1v1 = A2v2 to find am. When we calculate (8 x 0.5) divide by 2, we go get 2.0 m/s for the narrow side.

questions.q: A liquid flows through a uniform horizontal pipe such that the volume flow rate is 4.0 x 10⁻⁴ m³/s. If the cross-sectional area of the pipe is 2.0 x 10⁻⁴ m², what is the speed of the liquid in the pipe?
questions.e: Volume flow rate Q = Av, so v = Q/A = 4.0x10⁻⁴ / 2.0x10⁻⁴ = 2.0 m/s. This follows directly from the flow rate formula.
questions.p: To find the speed, we use formula Q = Av, where v = Q/A. If we divide 4.0 x 10⁻⁴ by 2.0 x 10⁻⁴, we go get 2.0 m/s straight.

questions.q: A small plastic ball is dropped into a tall column of glycerine. As it falls, its speed increases at first but soon becomes constant. Which of the following best explains why the speed becomes constant?
o: The upward viscous drag and upthrust together balance the weight of the ball
The weight of the ball reduces as it falls
Surface tension of the glycerine pulls the ball upward
The ball reaches the bottom of the container
questions.e: As speed increases, viscous drag (which depends on velocity) increases until, together with the upthrust, it balances the constant weight of the ball, giving zero net force and constant terminal velocity. Surface tension and weight loss are not relevant here.
questions.p: As the ball dey fall inside glycerine, the upward viscous drag and upthrust go join body balance the downward weight. Once dem balance, net force turn zero and the ball speed go con constant.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about surface tension is correct?
o: Surface tension acts perpendicular to the surface of a liquid
Surface tension decreases as the temperature of the liquid increases
Surface tension is greater in liquids with lower intermolecular forces
Surface tension causes liquids to have maximum surface area
questions.e: As temperature rises, molecules move faster and the forces of attraction between them weaken, so surface tension reduces. Surface tension actually makes liquids take up minimum surface area, not maximum, and it acts along (tangential to) the surface, not perpendicular to it.
questions.p: As temperature dey go high, molecules dey move fast and the attraction between dem dey weak, so surface tension dey reduce. Surface tension dey make liquid carry minimum surface area, and e dey act along the surface, no be perpendicular.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a steel needle, though denser than water, can float on the surface of still water when placed gently and horizontally?
o: The needle experiences upthrust greater than its weight
The needle displaces a volume of water equal to its own weight
The viscosity of water pushes the needle upward
The surface tension of the water supports the weight of the needle
questions.e: When placed gently, the needle does not break the surface film; the surface tension acts like a stretched elastic skin that supports the needle's weight. This is not due to upthrust (Archimedes' principle) since the needle is denser than water and would sink if submerged.
questions.p: If you drop am gently, the needle no go break the water surface film because surface tension dey act like rubber wey hold the weight. E no be upthrust because iron heavy pass water and suppose sink.

questions.q: A horizontal pipe carries water at a volume flow rate of 6.0 x 10⁻³ m³/s. The pipe has a wide section of radius 6.0 cm and narrows to a section of radius 2.0 cm. Calculate the speed of the water in the narrow section.
questions.e: Area of narrow section = π r² = π(0.02)² = 1.2566 x 10⁻³ m². Speed = flow rate / area = 6.0x10⁻³ / 1.2566x10⁻³ = 4.77 m/s, using the continuity equation.
questions.p: Area of narrow section na π r squared which be 1.2566 x 10⁻³ m². When you divide flow rate by this area, you go get 4.77 m/s using continuity equation.

questions.q: Two small soap bubbles of radii 2 cm and 4 cm are blown from the same soap solution. Which statement correctly compares the excess pressure inside each bubble?
o: The excess pressure is the same in both bubbles since they are made from the same solution
The excess pressure inside the smaller bubble is greater than that inside the larger bubble
The excess pressure inside the larger bubble is greater than that inside the smaller bubble
The excess pressure inside a bubble does not depend on its radius
questions.e: For a soap bubble, excess pressure is given by P = 4T/r, so pressure is inversely proportional to radius. The smaller bubble (2 cm) therefore has a greater excess pressure than the larger bubble (4 cm).
questions.p: For soap bubble, excess pressure na 4T over r, wey mean say pressure dey opposite to radius. So the smaller bubble wey get 2 cm radius go get higher excess pressure pass the 4 cm one.

questions.q: A student investigating fluid flow in a horizontal pipe observes that the flow is smooth and orderly at low speeds, with fluid particles moving in parallel layers that do not mix. At a certain critical speed, the flow suddenly becomes irregular and chaotic. What are these two types of flow called respectively?
questions.e: Smooth, orderly flow in parallel layers is called streamline or laminar flow, while flow above a critical speed, which becomes chaotic and mixes irregularly, is called turbulent flow. This change usually occurs at a critical velocity described by the Reynolds number concept.
questions.p: Smooth flow where liquid particles dey move for parallel layer na streamline or laminar flow. When speed pass critical point and e scatter, we dey call am turbulent flow.

questions.q: The main environmental concern associated with burning fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum to generate electricity is that it
o: increases the ozone layer thickness, cooling the earth
produces radioactive waste that remains dangerous for thousands of years
reduces the salinity of ocean water
increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, contributing to global warming
questions.e: Burning fossil fuels releases large amounts of carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that traps heat and causes global warming. Radioactive waste is linked to nuclear energy, not fossil fuels.
questions.p: When person burn fossil fuel, e dey release plenty carbon dioxide wey dey trap heat and cause global warming. Na nuclear energy produce radioactive waste, no be fossil fuel.

questions.q: A solar panel of area 2 m² receives solar radiation of intensity 800 W/m². If the panel converts this energy to electrical energy with an efficiency of 15%, what is the electrical power output?
questions.e: Total incident power = intensity x area = 800 x 2 = 1600 W. Electrical output = 15% of 1600 W = 0.15 x 1600 = 240 W.
questions.p: To find the power output, multiply intensity 800 W/m² by area 2 m² to get 1600 W total power. Then find 15% of 1600 W, and na 240 W you go get.

questions.q: In a thermal power station, chemical energy stored in fuel is converted to electrical energy through a sequence of energy transformations. Which of the following correctly represents this sequence?
o: Kinetic energy to chemical energy to heat energy to electrical energy
Heat energy to chemical energy to kinetic energy to electrical energy
Chemical energy to heat energy to kinetic energy to electrical energy
Chemical energy to electrical energy to heat energy to kinetic energy
questions.e: In a thermal power station, fuel burns to release heat energy, which boils water to produce steam that turns turbines (kinetic energy), and the turbine drives a generator to produce electrical energy.
questions.p: For thermal power station, fuel dey first burn to give heat energy, wey go boil water make steam turn turbine to kinetic energy. Na that turbine come make generator produce electrical energy.

questions.q: A nuclear reactor converts mass directly into energy according to Einstein's equation E = mc². If a reaction converts 2.0 x 10⁻⁶ kg of mass into energy, and the speed of light c = 3.0 x 10⁸ m/s, calculate the energy released.
questions.e: Using E = mc²: E = 2.0 x 10⁻⁶ x (3.0 x 10⁸)² = 2.0 x 10⁻⁶ x 9.0 x 10¹⁶ = 1.8 x 10¹¹ J. This huge energy release explains why nuclear fuel has very high energy density compared to fossil fuels.
questions.p: We use E = mc² formula, wey be 2.0 x 10⁻⁶ multiply by square of 3.0 x 10⁸. When you calculate am well, you go get 1.8 x 10¹¹ J.
